Normalize by mean curvature using P=p/H, Q=q/H, A=−1/(aH), B=−1/(bH). Two constraints give a regular autonomous system on a compact quarter-ellipsoid, topologically a disk; H decouples. The boundaries represent a Ricci-flat factor.
The analysis combines eleven-dimensional Killing-spinor equations, coset-invariant tensor/form algebras derived from structure constants, and four-dimensional supersymmetric F-term equations.

Reduction of the Ricci scalar and three-form kinetic term supplies scalar metrics; direct reduction of eleven-dimensional fermion terms supplies the gravitino mass matrix, from which gauging data and N=1 quantities are extracted.

Linearized fluctuations define background-dependent characteristic cones. Effective-metric analysis, boosted backgrounds and closed future-directed timelike trajectories diagnose failures of local evolution and global causal ordering.

Forward-amplitude contour integrals relate low-energy coefficients to discontinuities across physical cuts; crossing and the optical theorem turn these into positive total-cross-section integrals. A small scalar mass regulates infrared cuts and poles.
Large-volume expansions, canonical normalisation, and running-coupling estimates connect cycle volumes to decay constants and compare superpotential/Kähler instanton potentials with QCD.
The author analyses F-term equations and scalar-potential Hessians, using positivity of the Kähler metric to establish negative saxion curvature at the supersymmetric locus.

Kaluza–Klein reduction of bosonic kinetic terms determines the chiral metric. Reduction of ten-dimensional fermionic terms identifies W through the N=1 gravitino mass e^(K/2)W; spinor bilinears and Fierz identities convert the result into differential-form expressions.

Stable-form/pure-spinor geometry and Hitchin functionals organize the scalar spaces. Finite examples use bases with nondegenerate integrated antisymmetric Mukai pairing ⟨φ,ψ⟩=[λ(φ)∧ψ]₆, supplemented by prescribed nonclosure relations.
Use G=K+ln|W|² and the Killing-vector construction of field-dependent FI terms in gauged N=1 supergravity. Compare the D-term with the wrapped D7 world-volume action and induced D3-charge coupling.

Expand the scalar potential at large volume using the leading α′³ Kähler correction and string-loop corrections, then illustrate the combined F-term and D-term potential through numerical parameter choices.

Randomized free-fermionic boundary conditions and projection phases, subject to consistency constraints. Fermions are uniformly complex-paired and have only periodic or antiperiodic boundary conditions. Models are deduplicated using gauge groups and massless particle content.

Numerically evaluate the modular integral through a sum of net boson-minus-fermion degeneracies times integration kernels, including on-shell and off-shell states through at least approximately the fifth level, s≈5.
Compute regulated fixed-time geodesic lengths in global and Poincaré AdS3. For BTZ, a coordinate transformation to Euclidean AdS3 permits an analogous geodesic calculation.

Solve higher-dimensional minimal-area problems for a translationally invariant strip and a disk, using methods analogous to holographic Wilson-loop calculations. Expand areas in the UV cutoff and isolate finite or logarithmic terms.

Apply general supergravity tree-level soft-term formulae and add loop contributions. Explain intermediate-scale gaugino unification by matching beta-function-dependent high-scale splittings to renormalization-group running.

Expand W through cubic order around C = 0, T = T0. Use stationarity to express Taylor coefficients in terms of prescribed vacuum energy and supersymmetry-breaking parameters, then constrain remaining coefficients through the scalar Hessian.
Relate expansion to luminosity distance, including H(z)=[d(dL/(1+z))/dz]⁻¹ in flat FRW. Scalar-only examples reconstruct potentials and field histories from H and its time derivative.

Rewrite cosmological evolution as an autonomous system using normalized field variables and N=ln(a); locate critical points and classify their linear stability through Jacobian eigenvalues. Changing potential slopes are also treated through instantaneous critical points.

For membranes without fivebranes, use the imported Przanowski–Tod classification of four-dimensional quaternionic metrics with at least one isometry. The metric is governed by the continuous Toda equation (∂u²+∂v²)h+∂r²(e^h)=0; the resulting geometry is Einstein with anti-selfdual Weyl tensor.

Complete squares in the Euclidean double-tensor action to obtain two Bogomol’nyi bounds. For fivebranes, construct normalizable fermionic zero modes and a collective-coordinate measure, then infer effective kinetic terms and connections from two- and three-point correlators.

Anchor a bulk minimal surface on the brane horizon and identify it with a constant-Killing-time horizon section. Compare the resulting entropy with an equal-circumference flat-space circle using expansions in R/C_h.
Combine anomaly cancellation and Kähler-form curve-volume integrals with slope-stability inequalities, using equivariant stability of the pulled-back bundle on the covering threefold.

Construct the four-dimensional effective Kähler potential and superpotential from flux, hidden gaugino condensation, and membrane-generated worldsheet instantons. Solve D_F W=0 before uplift, then add the anti-five-brane potential and reconsider the equations of motion.

Numerically integrates dimensionless Euclidean field/gravity equations in Mathematica for a shifted quartic potential. Regular solutions are approximated by tuning the initial field value with regular-pole conditions; scans classify solutions by pass number.

Perturbs singular overshooting and undershooting solutions neighboring an instanton, avoiding direct perturbation of a regular geometry whose topology changes at VF=0. Counts barrier passes in the space of initial field values and potential shifts to locate regular-solution boundaries.

Uses the reviewed Coleman–De Luccia semiclassical prescription Γ∼exp[−(Sinst−Sbg)]. For nonpositive false-vacuum energy, a decay instanton must be noncompact and approach the flat or AdS false-vacuum background; compact regular solutions there do not describe decay.

Impose r_minus ≤ 1/Λ ≤ r_plus in dS and solve the resulting cutoff inequality; in AdS impose the nonblack-monopole condition together with a curvature-length requirement. An alternative dS estimate compares monopole mass with the Nariai mass scale L/G.

Compare string length with the horizon scale, then substitute brane tensions and compactification relations between Newton’s constant, string coupling, and string scale. Extend the estimates by replacing a single brane with a stack of N branes.

Numerically evolve all four real fields using canonical momenta and e-fold time; the authors also report direct second-order integration. Compute adiabatic power in an effective one-field approximation, P=H⁴/(50π²Lkin), evaluated at horizon crossing.

Construct the N=1 supergravity F-term potential and field-space metric from K and W. Slow-roll ε uses the metric-weighted gradient; η is the most-negative eigenvalue of the metric-raised covariant Hessian divided by V, preserving field-redefinition invariance.
Triple T-duality along x1, x2, x3 maps the specified toroidal IIB NSNS flux into a twisted IIA metric with H3=0, providing explicit examples for a brane dictionary.

Analyzes D6 deformations and gauge connections through a chain-integral superpotential; its Hessian involves integrals of ξi∧dξj. Physical masses require the induced Hodge-inner-product normalization of these forms.

Computes integral cohomology using integer combinations of invariant forms and the Maurer–Cartan differential, then obtains homology through universal coefficients and Poincaré duality. The cited justification for the integral invariant-form algorithm is restricted to the relevant two-step nilmanifolds.

Compare semiclassical potential-minimum estimates with numerical roots of throat-plus-bulk matching equations. Estimate compensator effects using second-order perturbation theory for a truncated dilaton/two-form system, whose perturbation Hamiltonian is non-Hermitian.

Linearize the 10D equations and reduce the simplified radial eigenproblem to a Schrödinger equation using dx=±e^(−2Ã)dr and δτ=e^(−3Ã/2)ψ. Solve the inverse-square throat potential with Bessel functions and impose boundary/interface matching conditions.

Uses holographic and AdS/CFT analogies to motivate a possible future-boundary description of outgoing FRW states and emergent time. This is a research proposal rather than a supplied nonperturbative construction.

Uses electron-loop power counting and equivalence-principle tests as litmus tests: a mechanism must distinguish vacuum energy from loop contributions to atomic or nuclear energies, and must address the particular electroweak vacuum.

Compares Hartle–Hawking weighting, de Sitter entropy, and Coleman–De Luccia tunneling suppression as selection proposals, then examines whether gravitational selection can operate in a matter-filled early universe.

Expands the charge and angular-momentum formulas at large center number N. Bubble equations constrain positions and are approximated explicitly for a distant center in the ring configuration; leading charge and JR estimates can be obtained without solving all positions.

Uses harmonic functions V and KI with common GH poles, self-dual dipole field strengths, and bubble fluxes Πij^(I)=kj^I/qj−ki^I/qi. Regularity and asymptotic conditions determine the remaining fields in the imported construction.
Estimates degeneracy through partitions of quantized flux parameters and, separately, a heuristic phase-space count treating neighboring bubbles as approximately rigid rods.

Differentiate the thermal canonical partition function with respect to the Euclidean metric to obtain stress-tensor means and connected correlators. Energy-density variance is related to heat capacity by ⟨δρ²⟩ = T² C_V/R⁶.

Use an imported closed-string density of states on a large three-torus, retaining the correction from the nearest partition-function singularity β₁ < β_H. Differentiate the resulting entropy to obtain temperature, heat capacity and pressure fluctuations.

Estimate the tensor spectrum using the scale-space Einstein relation k²h_ij ∼ 8πG δT_ij and the stress correlator. The treatment retains order-of-magnitude scaling rather than an exact transfer calculation.

Use period matrices and the Riemann bilinear identity; eliminate K and λ to obtain an induced-area action. Vary exact parts in ζ = [ζ] + dξ while holding cohomology fixed, producing harmonic-form equations.

Promote noncompact scalars to torus-valued maps, include winding classes in H¹(Σ_g,Λ), and gauge target translations. The abelian WZNW analog is a two-form B-field term, required for the global Chern-Simons identification.

Employ gauge Ward identities, geometric quantization, Narain-Siegel theta-function bases, Gaussian integration and propagator gluing to count states; study gravitational integration through expansions around classical attractor configurations.

ADM decomposition in comoving gauge, δφ=0 and h_ij=a²e^{2ζ}δ_ij, neglecting tensors. First-order lapse and shift solutions suffice for the cubic action. Integrations by parts and a nonlinear field redefinition remove redundant terms.

Interaction-picture commutator integrals compute the bispectrum. First-order corrections include Hankel-function mode corrections, time variation of couplings and the scale factor, Taylor-expanded around the sound-horizon exit of K=k1+k2+k3.

Bulk geodesic lengths and minimal-area variational problems yield interval, strip and disk results. The higher-dimensional intuitive argument assumes a twist-like insertion represented by a local diffeomorphism-invariant area integral; thermal entropy fixes its normalization.

Free strip calculations reduce transverse momentum modes to massive two-dimensional theories and integrate numerical entropic c-functions. Separately, replica conical geometry and the Weyl anomaly relate entropy scaling to four-dimensional central charges.
Replica path integrals use tr ρA^n=Zn/Z1^n and SA=−∂n log tr ρA^n at n=1. In two dimensions, twist operators, conformal maps and their conformal dimensions organize interval calculations.

Construct explicit Abelian-plus-SU(2) flux ansätze, calculate their Chern characters, and solve the resulting algebraic constraints. Three independent flux directions are subsequently used to constrain a general complex-structure matrix and Kähler form.
For the O3 choice θ=0, use the author's conditions J∧J∧J ch0(E)=J∧ch2(E) and J∧J∧ch1(E)<ch3(E). Compute induced charges from C4∧ch3(E)+C8∧ch1(E), then impose tadpoles and quantization.
Impose bundle holomorphicity F^(2,0)=0 and align the brane central-charge phase with the orientifold. The central charge used is the large-volume expression Z[E]=∫X e^(−iJ)∧ch(E).

Gauge invariance and stationarity of V_F+V_D+V_lift yield an auxiliary-field relation linking D_A, F-terms, the vector mass and uplifting derivatives. The paper extends a previously derived conventional-supergravity relation to include the Goldstino uplifting operator.

The analysis uses a chiral compensator, perturbations around supersymmetric AdS vacua, and an effective-supergravity description obtained through anomalous field redefinitions and integration of heavy matter/vector multiplets. Renormalization-group running relates high-scale soft terms to mirage masses.

Conformally map FRW to the unit static Einstein universe. Combine the integrated conformal anomaly with its renormalized Casimir energy and thermal free energy; for a scalar, F(η0)=Σn≥1 n² ln(1−e^(−nη0)).

Solve the anomaly-modified Friedmann equation together with mP²C=mP²B/2+F′(η0), where η0 is the full conformal-time period ∮N dτ/a. Radiation therefore depends nonlocally on the geometry it supports. Analytic limits and numerical solutions locate the instanton families.

Normalize the Euclidean density-matrix path integral by tr ρ=1. Integrate matter at one loop and evaluate the remaining lapse/scale-factor path integral at its effective-action saddle, thereby including the lowest-order quantum-matter back reaction.

Evaluate supergravity F-terms and D7 gaugino masses, then combine real-modulus and axion stationarity equations to identify a leading cancellation. Homogeneity arguments estimate the relative size of derivatives of Kähler-dependent prefactors and nonperturbative exponentials.

For the two-modulus example, expand the potential at large volume and use the Kähler metric and potential Hessian to estimate the heavy-modulus mass. Scalar masses follow from the standard matter-metric curvature formula.

Adopt an imported gauge and constraint treatment leaving a physical scalar perturbation. With norm proportional to ∫dσ a³(δφ)², derive a Sturm-Liouville Jacobi operator involving Q=1+κa²φ̇²/[2(l(l+2)−3K)].

Numerically shoot the coupled background equations by adjusting φ(0). Use Taylor expansions near the initial pole, impose a(0)=a(σmax)=0 and φ̇(0)=φ̇(σmax)=0, and normalize ȧ(0)=1. The second zero of a determines σmax.

Compute partial-wave determinant ratios with Gel'fand-Yaglom zero-eigenvalue initial-value solutions, using T=Φ/Φfv to obtain a finite endpoint ratio. Count negative modes through zeros of the corresponding Jacobi solution using the imported Morse theorem.

Compute the Maxwell Poisson kernel and its annihilator to identify symplectic leaves labeled by real magnetic/electric fluxes. Integration by parts gives commuting classical fluxes; quantization of a leaf uses a Fock representation and Hamiltonian polarization.

Use generalized differential-cohomology exact sequences, multiplication, and integration to construct a perfect pairing. Differential pushforward includes the characteristic form ÂE in its field-strength formula; Poincaré–Pontrjagin duality supplies nondegeneracy.

Define a Heisenberg extension of C(Y)×C(Y) using a pairing σ(A₁,A₂)=exp(2πi∫X F̃₁∧F̃₂), where connections extend over a bounding 4-manifold. Restriction to flat connections recovers the torsion linking pairing.

Derive the matrix description using DLCQ, a spacelike regulator preserving the dilaton background, a Lorentz transformation, and T- and S-dualities. The low-energy D1-brane worldvolume action gives 1+1-dimensional U(N) super-Yang–Mills theory.

Construct boost-invariant wavefunctions by superposing covering-space plane waves. Integrate the Virasoro–Shapiro four-point amplitude over boost parameters; the potentially divergent region is a Regge limit with large s and fixed momentum transfer.

Obtain the one-loop eigenvalue potential by integrating out off-diagonal fields through functional determinants. Use spin-dependent image propagators on the Milne worldsheet, a Schwinger-parameter representation, and modified-Bessel-function asymptotics.

Construct U(1) central extensions from alternating bimultiplicative commutators. Translation and multiplication operators furnish Heisenberg representations; Stone–von Neumann uniqueness and induction from maximal isotropic subgroups organize the Hilbert spaces. Infinite-dimensional uniqueness additionally requires a polarization, interpreted as positive energy.

Use curvature and characteristic-class exact sequences, their Bockstein map, differential-character products and integration, and smooth Poincaré–Pontrjagin duality. Flat fields can be topologically nontrivial; their identity component is a torus, with component group given by torsion cohomology.
Gauge-coupling and Planck-mass relations constrain geometric attempts to lower the decay scale. Worldsheet, membrane, and D-brane instanton actions estimate explicit PQ violation.
A low-energy chiral Lagrangian and gauged Wess–Zumino–Witten term provide a new derivation of the previously known pion contribution to the axion–photon coupling.

Dimensional reduction determines kinetic matrices from norms of harmonic forms; dualization of four-dimensional tensor fields determines scalar decay constants. Green–Schwarz and brane Chern–Simons terms determine quantized gauge couplings.
Compare explicit moduli-space metrics, geodesic distances and light spectra in compactification limits, including changes to Einstein frame and quotients by discrete dualities.

Estimate one-loop corrections to scalar kinetic terms after integrating out a generically heavy particle with moduli-dependent mass. The authors find that finitely many particles becoming massless do not themselves generate infinite distance for D > 2; an infinite tower can do so.

For Calabi–Yau vector moduli, analyze the integrated scalar curvature through the first Chern class and Kähler form, decomposing it into compactification and singularity contributions. Infinite-distance singularities are asserted to contribute negatively.
Apply Parke's gravitational thin-wall tunneling formulas and expand near the BPS threshold; separately solve coupled comoving-probability rate equations with absorbing decay currents.

Solve gravitino/modulino supersymmetry conditions for ds²=a²(r)(−dt²+dx²+dy²)+dr² and radial scalars; express the resulting first-order equations as gradient flows and, when W does not cross zero, warp-factor RG flows.

Complete the gravitational action, including extrinsic-curvature boundary terms, into BPS squares plus a total derivative. Integrate example flows numerically, including complex-structure and axion-dilaton evolution using Calabi–Yau periods.

The construction patches monopole potentials over two hemispheres and cancels their symmetric derivatives with ĥμν. A string-worldsheet coupling then measures a global phase through interference between lassoeing and non-lassoeing histories.
A Stückelberg decomposition hμν = ĥμν + ∂μAν + ∂νAμ exposes compensating gauge transformations and the additional polarizations introduced by the Pauli–Fierz mass.

The appendix eliminates Stückelberg fields through their linear equations, expressing effective actions using transverse projectors and inverse differential operators. This is an alternative presentation of the locally pure-gauge configurations.

Reduce the static two-dimensional field equations in conformal gauge, obtain w′=C exp(2φ), and impose C=0 to avoid an essential singularity. Analyze leading terms of separate weak- and strong-gravity expansions for the scalar and dilaton.

Rescale coordinates by μ and the scalar by a coupling-dependent power, then compare gravitational and scalar coefficients in the action. The potential-dependent exponent α controls the proposed coupling bound.
Use Wess–Zumino consistent anomalies for currents obtained from the effective action, insert the fermion connections, and analyze gauge variations of finite local counterterms.
Introduce a shifting Green–Schwarz chiral multiplet with axionic Chern–Simons couplings, then match coefficients of independent gauge and gravitational anomaly structures.

The review compares low-energy inflationary classes, examines whether moduli-stabilizing potentials preserve slow roll, and distinguishes genuine CMB deviations from changes in how microscopic parameters determine an inflaton potential.

Effective field theory organizes sensitivity to integrated-out high-energy states. Consistency filters include the absence of low-energy ghosts and instabilities and compatibility with solar-system and binary-pulsar tests.

DBI/Maxwell reduction supplies the inflaton kinetic normalization. Slow-roll parameters are evaluated with the canonical field; the stabilization analysis rewrites areas in terms of fixed supergravity moduli and applies the Einstein-frame Weyl rescaling.

The interaction is calculated from the open-string vacuum amplitude using a Coleman–Weinberg trace, oscillator sums and Poisson resummation. Removing the divergent zero mode gives a compact-torus Green function; the potential convention is Vint = −Areg.

Eliminate z_i using the full equations D_i[W_flux+W(T)]=0, obtaining generally nonholomorphic z_i(τ,T). Substitute into both K and W and work with the real function G=K+ln|W|²; the remaining supersymmetry equations are derivatives of G.

Use compatibility equations and real/imaginary decompositions to reduce complex-structure elimination to polynomial equations. Cases I and II involve cubics and Cardano solutions; case II further separates the Kähler-volume equations from the imaginary-dilaton equation. Case III requires a sextic.
An ADM action is organized in unitary gauge using residual spatial diffeomorphisms. The Stückelberg procedure restores π and exposes the derivative expansion and its kinetic and gradient signs.

Operators quadratic in lapse and extrinsic-curvature fluctuations modify the scalar dispersion. A full quadratic calculation solves lapse and shift constraints and substitutes them into the action for ζ, retaining gravitational mixing.

Expand around an equation-of-motion solution, construct the quadratic fluctuation Hamiltonian, and relate its kinetic matrix to the null-contracted stress tensor. Selected perturbations cancel additional derivative terms to expose negative kinetic directions.

For fluids, combine the sound-speed criterion with a second-order free-energy variation transferring matter between adjacent regions. Beyond fluids, use microcanonical/canonical ensembles and E=TS−pV.

Integrate out standard fermions using a Euclidean functional determinant; express the claimed NEC contribution as a nonnegative spectral sum. Treat a Weyl determinant through a corresponding Dirac determinant.

The imported construction reduces operators by field redefinitions, fixes invariant coefficients from heterotic input, and fixes c through consistency with a cited exact result. The present paper uses the resulting fields to extract an additional asymptotic scalar charge.

Integrate effective stress components radially from infinity, impose the asymptotic mass and time normalization, and retain the desired perturbative order. The operation converts the variational source into a metric without solving unrestricted higher-order differential equations.

Vary the action with respect to the gauge potential and metric, evaluate correction sources on the unperturbed background, solve for the electric-field response at fixed flux, and assemble the first-order stress tensor. Appendix A gives the explicit tensor expressions.

A superspace D-type spurion describes the redshifted uplifting brane. Tree-level moduli mediation is combined with anomaly mediation, followed by renormalization-group evolution to obtain the gaugino mirage pattern.

The author solves D_a W_eff=0 for a supersymmetric AdS configuration, then Taylor-expands the scalar potential and auxiliary fields around it. Minimization with an uplifting potential and nearly vanishing cosmological constant determines moduli shifts and induced F-components.
Base-2 entropy H and mutual information H(X)+H(Y)−H(X,Y) quantify intersection-number distributions and pairwise dependence; selected conditional distributions probe higher-order correlations.
Asymptotic integer counting uses divisor sums and Euler-totient/zeta corrections for primitivity, compared with explicit numerical enumeration.

Enumerate winding configurations using moduli-independent bounds, then solve linear supersymmetry conditions for common positive moduli. C-branes complete undersaturated tadpoles; this completion alone does not establish K-theory consistency.

Rindler reconstruction uses analytic continuation of boundary spatial coordinates. A second derivation Wick-rotates to de Sitter, uses its vacuum-independent retarded Green function, and analytically continues the scalar mass back.

Global normalizable mode sums are inverted and evaluated with hypergeometric identities. Fourier components absent from boundary data may be added to kernels without changing their convolution, allowing support to be rearranged.

A spacelike Green function gives an alternative even-dimensional global construction. Antipodal maps, frequency analyticity and contour arguments move global kernels into the Poincaré patch and establish covariance properties.

Spectrum calculations solve shifted-momentum masslessness equations and orbifold/Wilson-line projections; surviving roots and Cartan matrices identify gauge groups. Higher twisted sectors require eigenstate superpositions and additional projections.

Superpotential monomials are selected through vertex-operator correlators, gauge invariance, H-momentum/discrete R-charge rules and space-group matching. Gauge-invariant monomials characterize D-flat configurations; complexified gauge transformations are used to seek simultaneous F- and D-term cancellation. Precise coupling strengths are not calculated.

Reduce scalar propagation to a one-dimensional Schrödinger problem with potential U = a″/a. Reflection-coefficient poles and contour deformations organize the asymptotic terms. Supersymmetric quantum mechanics supplies a partner-potential argument for extending the pole structure beyond the explicit thin-wall example.

Compute scalar and graviton two-point functions on the Euclidean CDL geometry, analytically continue to the Lorentzian FRW region, and extrapolate toward Σ. This prescription selects Hartle-Hawking expectation values rather than independently specified Lorentzian boundary conditions.

Use minisuperspace Wheeler-DeWitt reasoning to motivate an expanding open-universe wave function whose leading late-time phase is proportional to regulated boundary area. Propose boundary variables (L, f), a local Hamiltonian constraint, and a measure |Ψ̂|² = exp[−S(L, f)].

Imported Gromov precompactness fixes dimension d and bounds diameter ≤ D and Ricci ≥ (d−1)k. The BBG spectral approach instead measures distances using Laplacian eigenfunction data, connecting convergence more directly to spectra and wavefunction overlaps.

Imported Cheeger finiteness theorem: bounded sectional curvature, a positive lower volume bound and an upper diameter bound yield finitely many diffeomorphism types of smooth compact manifolds in fixed dimension.

Variational and Dirichlet-ball comparison arguments bound scalar Laplacian eigenvalues using diameter and a Ricci lower bound. For nonnegative Ricci curvature, the comparison bounds decrease as D^-2 and extend to higher modes, supporting a KK-tower interpretation.

Use logarithmic S,T Kähler potentials and the standard supergravity F-term potential. Analyze stationary points of the full potential rather than first imposing supersymmetric AdS conditions and subsequently uplifting.
Search numerically for stationary points in (s,t,σ_S,σ_T), accepting local minima when all eigenvalues of the four-coordinate potential Hessian are positive.

Evaluate the gravitino mass, compactification volume, eleven-dimensional Planck scale, and condensation scales at the illustrative minima. Obtain visible-sector gaugino masses from moduli F-terms and derivatives of the visible gauge kinetic function, then quote their low-energy evolution.

Construct the four-dimensional supergravity scalar potential from a model Kähler potential and two nonperturbative exponentials. Solve Fᵢ = ∂ᵢW + (∂ᵢK)W = 0 for supersymmetric extrema, then exhibit nonsupersymmetric critical points numerically in a two-modulus example.

Identify when charged emission ceases to be exponentially suppressed, then impose M_discharge ≥ Qm so that sufficient rest energy remains to remove all charge. Combine this condition with RN horizon and extremality relations.

Separate hot-hole Hawking emission with an electric chemical potential from cold-hole Schwinger pair production. Extend the threshold estimates to higher-dimensional RN solutions; the cold-hole analysis also optimizes the proposed restriction over black-hole charge.

Couple a scalar with radial-dependent winding mass to gravity. Expand near the bubble wall in locally Cartesian coordinates and reduce the S-wave quadratic fluctuation problem to a shifted two-dimensional harmonic oscillator.

Review the Euclidean Schwarzschild construction of Witten's bounce and its analytic continuation to an expanding Lorentzian bubble; compare it with the static bubble obtained from lower-dimensional Euclidean Schwarzschild times a time direction.

Construct spherical, time-symmetric vacuum Cauchy data by solving the vanishing spatial scalar-curvature constraint. Impose absence of a conical singularity, f′_n(r0)=2/R, and use the ADM energy as a potential along the bubble-radius family.

Solve F-flatness DαW=0; the retained fields produce no D-term potential. Eliminating S,U leaves a real fifth-order condition Im(P2 P̄3)=0 and a twelfth-order real polynomial condition for τ, generally solved numerically.

Enumerate constrained even fluxes with absolute values bounded by N, fix modular redundancy using an upper-half-plane root of P2 or P3, and solve for stabilized vacua. Gauge-fixed sets reach N=30; the all-real-root sector receives a separate representative sample through N=20.

Expand Green's functions in normalized angular harmonics and radial modes. Wrapped-cycle integrals impose angular selection rules; Jacobi-polynomial identities and integration by parts establish cancellations. AdS/CFT identifies the surviving contributions with chiral and antichiral operators.

Solve the six-dimensional Poisson problem −∇²δh=C[δ⁶/√g−ρbg], with C=(2π)⁴gs(α′)² and normalized background charge, then integrate δh over the wrapped four-cycle to obtain its warped-volume correction.

The heterotic endpoint algorithm alternates lattice shifts and T-duality, temporarily absorbing Weyl transformations. Finite sequences, periodic tails and aperiodic sequences classify limiting behaviour; backtracking the initial endpoint determines dual Wilson lines when decompactification occurs.

An SL(2,Z) warm-up treats fixed-axion strong coupling as hyperbolic geodesic motion. Signed continued fractions encode reduction; for terminating expansions, reversing the coefficient sequence and negating its entries gives the dual axion.

The moduli geometry uses a Borel-gauge coset representative and Iwasawa decomposition. The inter-theory map is derived using explicit lattice bases, matched state masses, and simultaneous transformations of charges and moduli preserving mass and level matching.

For Kahler uplifting, expand the potential to leading order in a small correction, minimize the axion and real modulus, and illustrate with Casimir-inspired corrections from massless and massive bulk fields.

Expand around global-SUSY D-flat and F_chi-flat configurations. The leading D contribution requires second-order corrections to phi and first-order corrections to chi; T requires the full supergravity minimization. The naive zeroth-order F_T=0 ansatz fails.

Match unified gauge couplings and unification scales to compactification volumes. The unification-scale estimates assume discrete Wilson-line breaking and identify the scale approximately with an inverse cycle radius, including stated G2 threshold corrections.

Dimensional reduction of higher-form kinetic terms on normalized harmonic forms estimates axion decay constants; wrapped worldsheet, membrane and D-brane actions connect these constants to instanton suppression.
Estimate the species correction δMP²≈±NΛUV²/(16π²); requiring it below the tree contribution gives a multiplicity bound. The heterotic M-theory calculation takes ΛUV∼1/ℓ11.

Compute fluctuation determinants using S3 spherical harmonics and thermal Fourier modes, in covariant Rξ gauge with ξ=1. Integrate bosons, fermions, ghosts, nonconstant modes and off-diagonal homogeneous fluctuations to obtain a static one-loop potential.

At high temperature, approximate discrete spatial sums by momentum integrals. Around uniformly distributed holonomy eigenvalues, diagonalize the scalar quadratic form as a circulant matrix using discrete Fourier eigenvectors.

Analyze the near-vacuum supergravity potential through the superpotential Hessian W_ab. A seesaw argument and characteristic polynomial compare the one-complex-modulus conifold limit with a generic multi-modulus system.
Use the imported flux-vacuum count N_susy ∼ L_*^K/K!, Taylor-expand a narrow tadpole shell for uplifted vacua, and use Stirling-based estimates to relate the required vacuum count to K.

Evaluate Aharonov–Bohm phases on closed probe worldsheets or 2-brane worldvolumes. Continuous-deformation invariance and flux conservation constrain the profile f. An auxiliary two-form supplies a combed-monopole interpretation for spin-2 configurations despite the absence of an invariant spin-2 magnetic flux.

Construct topologically nontrivial but locally pure-gauge configurations using ξ5=0 and ξμ=f(y)Aμ, where Aμ has a Dirac-monopole potential. Expand f in KK harmonics; its coefficients are the proposed individual KK hair parameters.

Start from the reviewed supersymmetry classification, decompose forms into SU(3) representations, and read intrinsic torsion from dJ and dΩ. Impose supersymmetry, sourced Bianchi identities and form equations; Appendix B explicitly checks the dilaton and external Einstein equations.

Expand fluxes, harmonic gauge potentials and geometric forms in orientifold-adapted integral cohomology bases. Flux quantization, tadpole periods and algebraic supersymmetry relations determine vacuum values; the dual six-form relation supplies the constraint on C axions.
Solves effective field equations using static axial and spherical metric/gauge ansätze; evaluates Ricci components, horizon moduli relations and Hawking temperature through T_H = f′(r_h)/(4π).

Uses DBI-inspired brane dynamics, the Seiberg–Witten map, Moyal products and a background-field expansion of the effective metric. A block-diagonal 2+2 gauge choice and noncommutative scaling impose vacuum-field constraints to simplify the action.

Dimensional reduction expresses metric fluctuations and gravitino couplings through SU(3)/G2 structure forms and spinor bilinears. Contorsion is replaced by structure-form differentials; Weyl rescaling normalises the four-dimensional Einstein term.

The conifold action is constructed using N=2 Killing-vector gaugings and prepotentials. Dynamics are studied through homogeneous cosmological evolution and three-dimensional simulations with spatial inhomogeneities and induced gauge fields.

Construct commuting-spinor bilinears, apply Fierz identities, and translate vanishing fermion variations into first-order tensor conditions and spinor projections. The bilinears define a null vector and anti-self-dual quaternionic structures on a four-dimensional space.

Use Killing-spinor integrability to reduce the independent field equations. For the rotational ansatz φα=f(y²)yα and Arα=g(y²)ρrαβyβ, the remaining consistency condition becomes a third-order radial equation; the particular choice f=a/y² supplies the displayed solution.

Reduce homogeneous evolution to a lapse-dependent one-dimensional effective Lagrangian, equations of motion and constraint. With u=σ̇ and v=ϕ̇, either constant axion or spatial flatness permits a two-dimensional autonomous dynamical system.

Compactify the flat-model phase plane using x=u/v, y=1/v and dτ̂=|v|dτ. The constraint becomes x²+y²≤1. Analyze fixed points, their eigenvalues, separatrices and heteroclinic cycles; expanding and contracting systems occupy separate compactified hemicircles.

Transform with z = cos²(u/r0) to Gauss hypergeometric equations. Endpoint asymptotics, normalizability, current-conserving hermiticity conditions, and gamma-function pole conditions select wave functions and discrete radial quantum numbers n = 0,1,2,… .

Use light-cone gauge for physical vector fluctuations, angular Fourier decomposition, and radial field redefinitions to reduce vector and fermion equations to one-dimensional Schrödinger problems. Fermion first-order equations also constrain the paired chiral profiles.

Apply large-N factorization, conformal perturbation theory, stress-tensor correlation functions and double-trace beta functions. Use unitarity bounds and operator dimensions to constrain simultaneous couplings of several CFT factors.

Use Hamilton-Jacobi conjugate boundary data and Legendre transforms to extend the holographic generating functional. For W(p1,p2), sources obey qi+∂W/∂pi+αi=0, and the bulk functional contains I1+I2+∫[W−Σipi∂W/∂pi].

The field-theory calculation uses radial quantization, conformal perturbation theory and conformal-algebra descendant norms. The nonconserved spin-2 operator is chosen orthogonal to both the conserved total stress tensor and O1O2; its divergence norm determines its anomalous dimension.

The bulk calculation uses scalar propagators modified by mixed boundary conditions and their one-loop contribution to graviton self-energy. A bitensor decomposition isolates the transverse-traceless part; matching its long-distance massive spin-1 exchange structure extracts the mass. Tensor algebra was implemented in Mathematica.
Obtain connected stress-tensor correlators from metric variations of ln Z, with F=−β⁻¹ln Z. The density variance is T²C_V/R⁶; spatial stress fluctuations are related to derivatives of pressure.

Use the previously calculated closed-string density of states on a large three-torus, retaining the correction from the nearest partition-function singularity to β_H. For off-diagonal stresses introduce a small torus twist and set it to zero after differentiation.

For each comoving mode, evaluate thermal stress-tensor correlators at Hubble exit t_i(k), shortly before the transition. Use simplified Einstein constraints to infer scalar and tensor amplitudes, then evolve them with ordinary cosmological perturbation theory.

Solve D_SW=D_zW=0 using the full superpotential, including the nonperturbative term. Expand the resulting heavy fields in Ce^{-hT} and its conjugate; substitution generally produces a nonholomorphic function W(T,T̄).

Expand the invariant Kähler function through Λ, seek Λ=|W_eff|², and compare scalar potentials order by order. The toy model implements heavy-field elimination using real and imaginary components and an explicit second-order expansion.

Uses triple intersections and divisor Hodge data from toric resolutions; analyzes Euclidean D3 fermion zero modes through differential-form representatives, compatible κ-symmetry fixing and orientifold projectors.
Solves F-flatness equations, studies scalar Hessians through determinants and principal minors, and scans integer three-form fluxes subject to tadpole and vacuum-selection constraints.

Solve Q^t g Q = g and Q^t b Q = b to identify allowed metric and antisymmetric-tensor deformations; diagonalize the twist in complex coordinates and express untwisted moduli through lattice radii and angles.

Combine local compactifications, Stanley–Reisner exclusions, global divisor equivalences and fixed-set incidence data to determine intersection rings. Euler-number additivity, adjunction and Noether’s formula relate divisor topology to self-intersections and second-Chern-class pairings.

Construct crepant toric resolutions by adding lattice rays with fractional twist weights satisfying sum_i g_i = 1, then triangulating. Different triangulations can give different resolutions connected by flops; divisor stars identify local surface topologies.

The geometric construction uses a closed homothetic Killing vector k on the parent Kähler manifold and its associated Killing vector Jk; quotienting by dilatations and U(1) yields an n-dimensional Hodge-Kähler manifold. Supersymmetry Ward identities separately express scalar potentials through metric-weighted quadratic fermion shifts.

Superconformal construction: gauge the superconformal symmetry of a rigid supersymmetric parent, then fix the extra symmetries to obtain Poincaré supergravity. For n physical chiral multiplets, start with n+1, including a compensator whose modulus and phase are fixed by dilatations and U(1) R-symmetry.

Relate black-hole saddles to thermal AdS by modular transformations; use spectral-flow orbits and theta decompositions for charged states. Reconstruct the transformed elliptic genus from polar BPS data by summing inequivalent geometries in Γ∞\SL(2,Z).
Holographic renormalization: add Gibbons-Hawking and counterterms, use a Fefferman-Graham expansion, and extract the boundary stress tensor and central charge from its Weyl anomaly.

Anomaly inflow and dimensional reduction determine Chern-Simons coefficients. Supersymmetry relates an SU(2) level to its central charge by c=6k; the gravitational coefficient β fixes c−c̃=96πβ. This avoids needing the full higher derivative action in the protected examples.

Solve twisted closure of the weighted first pure spinor, construct a compatible second spinor with closed weighted real part, and obtain RR fields from its weighted imaginary part. Supersymmetry alone is insufficient: the remaining flux equations and Bianchi identities must also hold.

Use Maurer–Cartan equations to reduce invariant differential conditions to algebraic ones. For the algebraic solvable-group compactness test, seek an adapted rational basis for which P(G)/P(G)Z is compact; failure in one basis is insufficient.

Match the invariant-form components of (d−H∧)F to smeared calibrated sources. Required source volume forms are closed and decomposable; this is stronger than merely demanding source exactness in twisted cohomology.

Invert the supergravity relation Ŷαβγ=e^(K̂/2)Yαβγ/(K̃αK̃βK̃γ)^(1/2). When a modulus is absent from the holomorphic Yukawas, its physical-Yukawa scaling constrains the corresponding matter-metric scaling.

In the dilute-flux approximation, reduce the D7 DBI action to super Yang–Mills and express physical Yukawas as overlaps of normalized internal wavefunctions. Rescaling their support volumes determines leading powers without evaluating complete Calabi–Yau wavefunctions.

A Dirac index on the real two-dimensional intersection counts chiral bifundamentals. The imported Veneziano–Yankielowicz–Taylor description, with the gaugino bilinear integrated out, supplies the ADS superpotential used for the gauge-invariance comparison.

Dimensional reduction of the bosonic DBI action, using calibration conditions and an expansion near supersymmetry, extracts the D-term and gauge coupling. Reduction of Chern–Simons couplings identifies axion gauging and checks relative signs through holomorphic gauge kinetic functions.

Power-count the longitudinal scalar's leading cubic interaction, whose stated momentum dependence is (r_c k)^[4(1−α)] k². Balance nonlinear and linear contributions to estimate r_*, then match interior and exterior scalar behavior.

Introduce Stückelberg fields, derive their constraint, and integrate out the extra polarizations to isolate a two-tensor effective equation. Compare its exchange amplitude with the full amplitude coupled to conserved sources.
Use a Euclidean spectral representation Δ(k²)=∫ds ρ(s)/(k²+s), with bounded nonnegative spectral density, to constrain the infrared propagator and hence α.

Compute the metric-dependent flux energy schematically as ∫F∧*F and regard it as a potential on moduli space. Use dimensional reduction and Weyl rescaling to obtain the four-dimensional Einstein-frame description.

Illustrate vacuum counting by integer flux vectors satisfying Σn_i²≤L, approximating lattice counts by high-dimensional volumes when the flux region is sufficiently large. This cutoff is a toy substitute for actual tadpole constraints.

Combine supergravity with α′ and string-coupling corrections, semiclassical instantons and wrapped branes. Holomorphy, mirror symmetry and string duality constrain protected quantities and leading nonperturbative superpotential contributions.
Use a monopole as a probe of the gauge-theory cutoff. Compare its size L_mon ∼ 1/Λ with its d-dimensional black-hole radius, using R_bh^(n+1)(M) ∼ M_d^(-(n+2)) M, and require L_mon > R_bh(M_mon).

Give an alternative force argument by comparing four-dimensional gauge repulsion with higher-dimensional gravitational attraction, then evaluate the constraint at a separation of order the charged particle's Compton wavelength.

Evolve string-scale boundary conditions using SoftSUSY2.0; use micrOmegas1.3 for relic density and flavour observables, and scan charge/colour-breaking directions including UFB3. These are historical phenomenological calculations.

Insert moduli F-terms and imported chiral matter metrics into N=1 supergravity soft-term formulae. Compute both diagonal and non-diagonal matter metrics, then canonically normalise to obtain physical masses and trilinears.

The inflaton kinetic term is treated with the Dirac–Born–Infeld action, reducing to the standard kinetic term in slow roll. COBE normalization reduces the slow-roll model to a one-parameter analysis; a finite field range and the Lyth bound constrain tensor predictions.

Reviewed microscopic methods include open/closed-string channel duality, an open-string one-loop sum grouped by softly broken supermultiplets, and boundary superstring field theory for the brane/tachyon potential. These are reported methods, not calculations reproduced here.

The analysis uses the interior FRW Einstein equation H²=κρ−k/R², compares density with ρc=H²/κ, and rewrites it as Ṙ²−κρR²=−k. This supplies the authors' kinematic argument for positive-curvature initial data consistent with energy conservation.

A rough conditional-probability estimate multiplies tunneling rates by counts of suitable potential regions: P(CDL|us)/P(B*|us)∼[Γ(CDL)/Γ(B*)][N(60+)/N(B*)]. Here 'us' means a large, nearly flat universe admitting structure formation.
Use the GVW superpotential W=∫G∧Ω with W=∂φW=∂τW=0, supplemented by primitivity J∧G=0. The integrated five-form Bianchi identity constrains the allowed flux-induced D3 charge.

Solve magnetic-flux holomorphicity, DBI calibration/D-flatness and positive gauge-coupling conditions together with R–R tadpole cancellation. Charged scalar contributions deform the zero-VEV FI equations.
Couple the EFT to Einstein gravity and analyze scalar perturbations in longitudinal gauge, setting α2 = 0 for simplicity, to obtain the stability criterion.
Construct the unitary-gauge EFT from residual symmetries, then restore broken transformations and identify their gauge parameter with the Nambu–Goldstone field π.
For an imported four-parameter supergravity solution family, impose horizon regularity using the Ricci and Kretschmann scalars, reducing the family to two parameters.

Expand D-brane DBI/CS actions to quadratic order and compare flux-generated potentials with kinetic normalization. Match the resulting warp dependence to 4D Kähler potentials and standard auxiliary-field expressions for soft masses.

KK eigenmode analysis and energetic localization arguments estimate bulk versus throat mass scales. An explicitly reducible massive scalar on a finite AdS5 interval with Neumann boundaries illustrates wave-function mixing and degenerate perturbation theory.

General P(X,φ) perturbation theory supplies sound-speed-dependent scalar and tensor spectra, r=16c_sε, and a generalized field-excursion integral. Equilateral non-Gaussianity and scalar-amplitude formulas constrain quadratic DBI models.
The imported Lyth relation is written as r_CMB=8(Δφ/MP)²/N_eff², with N_eff the integral of √(r/r_CMB) over e-folds from CMB quadrupole exit to inflation's end.

Dimensional reduction and integration of the warped internal volume provide a lower bound from the throat alone. This is combined with canonical radial normalization φ²=T3ρ² and the maximal radial displacement.

Estimate decay using a triangular barrier approximation, Sb∼(Δχ)⁴/ΔV. Obtain tree-level soft terms from general supergravity expressions involving Kähler curvature, auxiliary fields and gauge kinetic functions.

Search for supersymmetric solutions using a block-field ansatz and D_i W=0. In the gauged magnetic theory, integrate out massive quarks to obtain a determinant-dependent nonperturbative superpotential.

Expand the supergravity potential in hidden fields divided by MP and linearize stationarity around the ISS–KKLT vacuum. Include Coleman–Weinberg one-loop corrections because tree-level pseudomoduli otherwise obstruct this linearization.

For toroidal examples, solve a linearized warp-factor Poisson equation with compact-space charge compensation, average its Green function over the wrapped cycle, and sum orbifold images. The holomorphic result involves logarithms of Jacobi theta functions.

Evaluate the supergravity F-term potential, analyze the small-angle mass matrix, and minimize angular variables. Derive an additional probe-D3 potential from DBI and Chern–Simons terms with a perturbed dilaton.

Boundary/cross-cap CFT and modular transformations relate open-string loop amplitudes to closed-string exchange. Massless-exchange divergences diagnose tadpoles; relative annulus/Möbius phases determine Chan–Paton projections.

Dimensional reduction of DBI and Chern–Simons actions supplies gauge and axionic couplings. Homology and intersection pairings organize charge constraints and chiral spectra; four-dimensional N = 1 supergravity organizes scalar metrics, holomorphic gauge kinetic functions, and F-/D-term potentials.

Uses anomaly-canceling Wess–Zumino couplings S_WZ = ∫_N C ∧ ch(E) ∧ sqrt(Â(TN)/Â(NN)) to identify induced lower brane charges. The Freed–Witten discussion uses the coefficient exact sequence 0 → Z → Z → Z2 → 0, with multiplication by two, and its Bockstein W3 = β(w2).

Uses the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence to remove inconsistent cohomology classes and quotient unstable charges. Its first relevant differential is d3 = Sq^3 + H∪; higher differentials can matter. With real coefficients, d_(2n+1)(x) is expressed as a Massey product of n copies of H with x.

The search usually fixes complex structure at the Fermat point, solves supersymmetry and orientifold invariance as linear equations in integral fluxes, and imposes a positive quadratic tadpole bound. Integral and Hodge-adapted bases trade straightforward quantization against simpler tadpole expressions.

A-branes are described using vanishing-cycle wedges, B-branes using polynomial matrix factorizations Q²=W·id. Open-string Witten indices give intersection pairings; permutation branes and crosscap overlaps supply integral charge bases and orientifold charges.

Use holomorphic changes of nondynamical couplings to connect strongly coupled configurations to independent conifolds. Interpret conservation of vacuum number through the chiral ring, where idempotents may become nilpotents while the stated total number of generators remains fixed.

Reduce threefold periods and the flux superpotential to differentials on the punctured curve; regulate noncompact periods, include the puncture modulus, and use special Kähler curvature to obtain the vacuum-counting density.

Studies large-volume asymptotics of nonperturbative and α′ contributions, then estimates omitted higher-derivative effects through dimensional-reduction volume scalings rather than their unknown full tensor structure.

Uses four-dimensional N=1 supergravity, V=e^K(K^{i j̄}D_iW D_j̄W̄−3|W|²), with flux superpotentials computed from periods in a symplectic basis. Dimensional reduction fixes the physical superpotential prefactor.

Reviews the imported Ashok–Douglas signed index density proportional to det(−R−ω), derived through a continuous Gaussian flux ensemble and inverse transform. Tests use Monte Carlo integer fluxes, numerical root finding and truncated period expansions.

Further filters require an unsuppressed renormalisable top Yukawa and maximal-rank exotic mass matrices from string-allowed superpotential terms through order eight. Singlet insertions generate masses of the form x_i x̄_j⟨s_a s_b…⟩.

Uses gauge-lattice symmetries to generate the approximate inequivalent-model denominator. Equivalence is defined by identical non-Abelian spectra and equal numbers of non-Abelian singlets, without distinguishing all U(1) charges.

Enumerates Wilson lines and filters successively for GSM⊂SU(5)⊂SO(10) or E6, three net quark doublets, non-anomalous SU(5) hypercharge, and three net SM families with Higgs candidates and vectorlike extra matter.

Combine classical scalar–FRW evolution with the imported modification H² = ρ(1 − ρ/M_pl⁴)/(3M_pl²). To apply this originally flat-universe equation inside the open bubble, the authors count curvature as an effective density 3M_pl²/a².
Treat vacuum decay as first-order bubble nucleation using a thin-wall instanton criterion. The initial bubble radius and decay probability are explicitly set aside.

Dimensional reduction and Weyl rescaling determine the 4d Kähler potential and gauge kinetic function. The authors compare direct integration of the flux energy with the supergravity D-term obtained from the modulus Killing vector.

Charged spectra are treated using harmonic-oscillator algebra, the squared Dirac operator and the two-dimensional index theorem. Orbifold parity counting determines surviving towers; dimensional regularization and Hurwitz/Riemann zeta functions evaluate their one-loop determinants.

Reduce the Einstein term to scalar sigma-model metrics, compare metric-parameter kinetic terms with those of B-field scalars, and use algebraic Hodge identities to recover special Kähler and quaternionic geometry under the imposed conditions.
Use compact-manifold Laplacian spectral theory to characterize finite expansion systems, then construct a normalized massive-eigenform example and examine changes of symplectic basis.
Use background-field gauge, include Faddeev–Popov ghosts, expand to quadratic order, and successively perform Gaussian integrations over gauge and scalar fluctuations.
Square the Dirac operator and treat the additional operator V through a trace expansion. Gamma-matrix trace identities remove its gamma-dependent terms from the vacuum determinant.

Solve fluctuation eigenvalue equations in weighted orthonormal bases and evaluate determinants with Schwinger proper time. Integration over the momentum q produces δ(2sp), localizing the remaining trace at p=0.
Integrate out the relatively heavy fields φ1,φ2 of W=mφ1φ2+λSφ1²−µ²S, and represent Coleman–Weinberg one-loop effects through a small-field expansion of the effective Kähler potential for S.
The authors use Mathematica to construct the supergravity scalar potential, expand at small S and in x near the original AdS volume minimum σ0, and present numerical parameter examples.

Construct a naive massless-IIA-to-M-theory lift, then impose Bianchi, Einstein and supersymmetry conditions. The required weak G2 structure obeys dφ3=4m *7φ3 and implies Ricmn=6m²gmn; this supplies a consistency criterion rather than an explicit corrected metric.

Apply approximate T-dualities along x1 and then x2, converting H3 into geometric twisting and eliminating F0. A gauged worldsheet U(1) example tracks the orientifold through the duality; wrapped cycles are followed through their Poincaré-dual forms.

Use AdS black-hole entropy S=A_Einstein/(4G4), followed by CFT thermodynamics, to compare flux-dependent entropy with M2-brane scaling. The paper also compares entropy before duality, after double duality and in the naive eleven-dimensional lift.
The imported cutoff argument uses a heuristic magnetic-monopole estimate m ∼ Λ/g² together with the magnetic bound m < Mp/g to motivate Λ < g Mp.

The new argument combines a Compton-wavelength localization criterion, an EFT mass cutoff, and the AMNV cutoff bound, then reasons qualitatively about how the eligible particle species change as the black-hole mass decreases.

For scalar examples at sufficiently large θ, approximate the energy by its potential contribution, solve dV/dφ = 0, and insert the resulting soliton energy into the three-dimensional deficit-angle condition 8πG3E ≤ 2π.

Use known noncommutative soliton tensions or energies as gravitational sources. For the four-dimensional monopole with an attached semi-infinite string, impose a ceiling of 2π on the string-induced deficit angle 8πG4T.

Gauge the fibre coordinate through dψ→dψ+A and deform the four-form flux, then substitute into the eleven-dimensional equations. Projected gravitino variations supply the fermionic extension. Thermal observables are imported through charged-black-hole thermodynamics and stress-tensor Kubo analysis.
Identify four-cycle bases, impose integral four-form periods, fix geometric parameters and L, and evaluate the warped-volume formula for the holographic central charge.

Construct a generalized calibration from Killing-spinor bilinears, identify calibrated membrane cycles and evaluate their warped volumes. Explicit κ-symmetry calculations provide an additional check for the Kähler–Einstein examples.

Compute a fitted coefficient's dimensions, solve for powers of the allowed constants, and retain any unmatched dimensional factor. Only then define a dimensionless normalization. This operation separates dimensional admissibility from the additional empirical and physical assumptions needed for universality.

For δGS=0, analyze dilaton stationary conditions and the leading Hessian at large xa=2SR(3ka/2βa), supplemented by numerical minimization. Realistic candidate minima satisfy 2SR WS−W=0; WS≈0 is a further weak-coupling approximation.

Choose symmetrized potential jets and their δ-images as contractible pairs, leaving ghosts and covariant curvature jets. The remaining calculation uses Lie algebra cohomology with polynomial coefficients and its invariant-submodule decomposition.

PQ quality is estimated using dimension-(4+n) operators suppressed by MP^n, dimensional analysis of the induced axion potential, and the requirement that the resulting displacement satisfy δθ < 10^-9.
