Use T-duality in nine Euclidean dimensions to map multiply wrapped world-lines of charge-n D-particles to D-instantons of charge mn. Poisson resummation and a K₁ Bessel-function expansion analyze the proposed modular coefficient.

Apply the sixteen broken supersymmetries to generate fermionic zero modes, integrate over translational and Grassmann collective coordinates, and use LSZ reduction. String counterparts are disks with one closed-string insertion and fermionic open-string zero-mode insertions; nonzero leading amplitudes saturate sixteen Grassmann modes.
The appendix dualizes C^(0) to an eight-form potential, completes the Euclidean action into a positive square plus a boundary term, and obtains a Bogomol'nyi bound saturated by the BPS solution.

Expand R=Rc+r, N=1+n and D=Dc+d, retain the bilinear action, and impose n=0. The coupled r–d system is restricted by an assumed linear relation instead of being diagonalized into independent canonical variables.

Reduce the restricted fluctuation equation to hypergeometric form using y=Rc^−4 and r=Rc^−p ψ(y). Apply endpoint finiteness, reflection parity and weighted square integrability; the latter is estimated using a beta-function integral.

Replace the axion description by a conserved current with fixed wormhole charge Q, reduce to radial equations, integrate the D equation using a neck condition, and obtain the radial background equation. Numerical integration is used to illustrate the background.

Use the sufficient curvature-regularity condition that e^−A, ρ/χ and χ̇/χ remain finite. Combine it with asymptotic power-law or exponential solutions near χ→0 and with a phase-by-phase analysis of the evolution.

Rather than obtain arbitrary exact solutions, integrate the dilaton equation once as χ̇=e^−3A(σ+c), introduce K to relate A and χ, and follow signs and turning points. K=1 locates scale-factor extrema; σ+c=0 locates dilaton extrema.

Compute quartic gauge anomalies using representation trace identities, then seek factorization into sums of real squares. Tensor-scalar couplings to tr F² cancel the factorized anomaly and determine scalar-dependent inverse gauge couplings.

Use hyper-Kähler quotient quivers, index-theorem instanton dimensions including boundary η-invariant contributions, Higgs-branch dimension counts and flat directions describing instantons leaving the singularity. Matching dimensions and these motions supplies evidence for proposed moduli-space identifications.

Project a consistent left-right symmetric closed spectrum by world-sheet parity. Transform Klein-bottle, annulus and Möbius amplitudes into closed-string exchange channels; factorization turns massless tadpole cancellation into linear equations for Chan-Paton multiplicities.

Use rational-CFT characters, modular S transformations and fusion coefficients to build annulus amplitudes. In the canonical diagonal construction, the Verlinde formula gives transverse-channel coefficients as perfect squares of boundary reflection combinations.

Analyze the residual quadratic anomaly polynomial using multiple tensor Chern-Simons couplings. The reviewed supergravity equations were obtained either through supersymmetry requirements or Wess-Zumino consistency, producing covariant or consistent anomaly currents respectively.

Describe Landau-Ginzburg chiral operators through the Jacobian ring C[Φ_i]/(∂_iW). The single-field potential W=Ψ^{P+2} is related, conditional on its infrared fixed point, to the A-invariant N=2 minimal model with c=3P/(P+2); projected tensor products reach the desired central charge.

Use N=2 operator products, highest-weight representations and positive anticommutators. These give h≥Q/2, chiral saturation h=Q/2, and h≤c/6 for chiral primaries; their nonsingular operator products close into a finite ring for a nondegenerate theory.

Encode divisors and intersections in toric fans and hypersurface monomials in lattice polyhedra. Secondary fans organize regions through triangulations and asymptotic dominance of discriminant monomials, allowing comparison of complex-structure and enlarged Kähler moduli spaces.
Use homogeneous-coordinate weights for toric bases and, more generally, first-Chern-class bookkeeping with f and g sections of L⁴ and L⁶. The auxiliary double cover has ξ valued in L and h in L².
For bases F_n, inspect which polynomial coefficients are allowed and test singularity by simultaneous vanishing of the double-cover equation and its first derivatives.

Factor the discriminant in the special family, follow j(λ) on weak-coupling contours, and determine SL(2,Z) monodromies. The real-part shift initially determines ±T⁻⁴; solving for the two conjugates of T fixes the product to −T⁻⁴.

Start from transformation and field-equation ansätze with unknown coefficients, impose supersymmetry closure modulo field equations, and require equations to transform into one another. Closure on bosons already uses tensor duality equations; the construction is not an off-shell closure argument.

Use coset geometry, Maurer–Cartan decompositions, supercovariant field strengths, gamma-matrix dualities and Fierz rearrangements. Gauging follows the ungauged construction by covariantizing derivatives and adding the required C^{AB}-dependent gaugino transformation and equation terms.

Reduce the M5 chiral tensor using square-integrable harmonic one-forms, relate the resulting couplings to Jacobians, and organize curve deformations plus line bundles as complex integrable systems. Elliptic models additionally use Riemann–Roch and residues of meromorphic differentials.

Determine holomorphic curves from brane counts, asymptotics, and absence of semi-infinite D4-branes. Polynomial degree counts fivebranes; coefficient degrees encode D4 counts. With D6-branes, demanding finite y and z at finite v imposes polynomial divisibility conditions.

Solve the asymptotic fivebrane Laplace equation to obtain logarithmic bending. Finite kinetic energy constrains sums of D4 positions, freezing U(1) differences; relative fivebrane bending is interpreted as logarithmic gauge-coupling running.
Use generalized Weierstrass equations, Tate's algorithm, and holomorphic coefficient sections ai,σ in O(2i+D²i−D²σ) to constrain singular fibers and construct local models.

Embed the gauge group into a larger group with trivial relevant homotopy, relate global determinant phases to its local anomaly through an exact homotopy sequence, and modify the descent form to include the Green–Schwarz contribution.

Use Chan–Paton orbifold/orientifold representations and affine SU(M) Cartan relations. Extract irreducible anomaly terms from tadpole expressions linear in ranks and reducible terms from rank bilinears; infer tensor–gauge couplings.

Track volume factors in divergent cylinder, Möbius-strip and Klein-bottle amplitudes using Neumann momentum and Dirichlet winding sectors; distinguish untwisted and twisted tadpoles before taking infinite volume.

Factor reducible six-dimensional gauge anomalies into sums of real squares to determine tensor couplings. Construct Chan–Paton orientifold actions and extract anomaly coefficients from twisted tadpoles; count closed-sector tensors using inverse conjugacy classes.

Use hyper-Kähler quotients, affine ADE quivers, character orthogonality, and index theorems with boundary eta invariants to compare instanton and Higgs-branch dimensions. Frobenius–Schur indicators organize real, pseudoreal and complex representations.

Resolve Weierstrass collisions by base blowups and minimalization preserving K_X=0. Kodaira vanishing orders and monodromy determine gauge algebras; required base blowups count tensors. For simple Spin(32)/Z₂ instantons, resolve the branch curve of u²=p(s,t).

Take semistable then stable degenerations, using base changes, blowups and blowdowns. Identify the heterotic elliptic curve or K3 through intersections of degeneration components; separate geometric moduli from point-like-instanton data.

Wilsonian derivation combines one-loop holomorphic gauge-kinetic renormalization with the anomalous path-integral Jacobian required to restore canonical chiral normalization. Holomorphy, θ periodicity and composition of cutoff changes constrain the holomorphic contribution.

A second presentation integrates the NSVZ β-function, uses multiplicative wavefunction factors, and converts couplings through 8π²/gh²=8π²/gc²+CA ln(gc²). The authors explicitly state that this presentation is closely related to, rather than independent of, the Wilsonian argument.

Use holomorphy and discrete axion shifts to constrain gauge kinetic functions; match Green–Schwarz couplings and Bianchi identities to their coefficients, and compare with the strong-coupling boundary-volume expansion.
Integrate out hidden gauge and matter multiplets, then estimate axion potentials from the supergravity scalar potential and quadratically divergent one-loop supertrace contributions.

Spectrum construction uses orbifold gauge-lattice shifts and Wilson lines, modular invariance M(V²−v²)∈2Z for M=2,3,4,6, and bundle index-theorem calculations. Gauge and gravitational anomalies serve as consistency tests and constraints on candidate transitions.

Geometric analysis uses elliptic equations y²=x³+fx+g, singularity types, polynomial-deformation counts and Hodge numbers. Blow-ups and blow-downs of the base describe tensor branches and transitions between Hirzebruch surfaces.

Mass-deforming finite N=4 or N=2 theories supplies explicit holomorphic regulators. Matching the regulator masses under field rescaling, including Mc=Mh gc², yields the coupling relation in these schemes.

Rescaling Jacobians are evaluated with regulated component heat kernels, retaining auxiliary fields and gauge-fixing contributions. Instanton backgrounds and zero-mode counting isolate the holomorphic F-term; superspace formulations provide complementary descriptions.

Holomorphy, θ periodicity and continuity constrain the holomorphic beta function to a Fourier expansion. Weak-coupling regularity excludes negative Fourier indices; positive indices represent possible nonperturbative terms.

Canonical critical behavior is used to extract large-mass microcanonical information. Lowest thermal-scalar eigenvalues determine the density of states, while scalar correlation functions recover the random-walk size.

A self-consistent mean-field treatment first solves the string in a fixed background, then sources the background with averaged string stress energy. Weak-field reduction gives a nonlinear Schrödinger equation whose variational functional is studied by scaling.

Test a dangerous quartic-curvature counterterm through linearized N=2 superfields and variation of the conformal prepotential, using the BPS extreme Reissner–Nordström condition in an asymptotically weak-field region.
Establish the nonlinear group action by composing charge-dependent rotation and scaling factors. Identify charge spectra as homogeneous spaces using the strict-Borel stabilizer of a reference charge.

Use an Iwasawa decomposition adapted to the vacuum and charge vector. A Borel transformation restores the scalar moduli after a standard G transformation, and a trombone compensator restores the intended charge normalization.

Anomalous Abelian generators are rotated into a single trace-weighted combination. Cancellation of the induced Fayet–Iliopoulos term is analyzed together with the remaining D-flatness conditions and Fα = ⟨∂W/∂Φα⟩ = 0.

The kinetic-mixing discussion diagonalizes the gauge terms by a vector-field shift and tracks induced charges, gaugino couplings and D-terms. The reported scalar-mass correction is (m²a)KM = gi χ Qia ⟨Dk⟩, retaining its charge-dependent sign.

The analysis uses hidden-sector condensation scales Λhid ∼ MPl exp(−2πkS/b), a sum Weff = MPl³ Σa Ca(T)exp(−6πkaS/ba), and the associated supergravity scalar potential to estimate stabilization and supersymmetry-breaking scales.

For the high-scale supersymmetric stage, the authors impose simultaneous holomorphic equations Weff = ∂TWeff = 0. They state that a solution is automatically a local scalar-potential minimum with unbroken supersymmetry and zero cosmological constant; global minimality depends on the Kähler function.

The winding-field argument combines Fourier decomposition of the localized H-monopole, T-duality, semiclassical world-sheet disk amplitudes, and a truncated point-source effective theory. The last solves a massive flat-space Laplace equation for the asymptotic winding profiles.

A topological contraction is exhibited by the trajectory x5 = 2πRσ, θ = πτ, φ = −2πσ, r = r0. At the south pole the regular coordinate x̄5 = x5 + Rφ vanishes, displaying unwinding at fixed, arbitrarily large radius.

Dimensional reduction of the gravity–dilaton–B-field action with string sources yields gauge currents containing both bulk-field and world-sheet contributions. The analysis follows their radial charge inflow and couples the string to a monopole B-field collective coordinate.

Canonical analysis identifies electric fluxes, charge quantization and effective tension. The supersymmetric calculation uses Lie derivatives of pulled-back forms, superspace torsion constraints, and separate dimension-zero and dimension-one-half variations.

Package the real field strengths into the complex quantity F=U^rF_r and its scalar density Φ=(1/2)ε^{ij}F_ij. Use the SU(1,1) Maurer–Cartan forms P,Q and a U(1)-covariant Bianchi identity to maintain manifest covariance.

Track SL(2,Z) monodromies using branch cuts, enforce charge conservation at junctions, and apply brane-crossing moves that create or remove prongs. Glue compatible endpoints and slide or collapse junctions to obtain alternative representatives and products.

Decompose exceptional adjoints under manifest subalgebras and match representations to endpoint configurations. Analyze selected geodesics using a string-tension-weighted metric, locally the modulus squared of an analytic one-form, and conical limits.

Trace horizons through (∇φ)²=0 and distinguish metric perturbation σ from horizon perturbation δ. Analyze early Lorentzian evolution by power series; impose regularity on a compact Euclidean geometry and analytically continue complex perturbations to late Lorentzian time.

Vary the localized effective action in conformal gauge, solve Z=2ρ+η with ∂²η=0, and use Fourier modes on the initial S¹ to discuss the constraints. Linearize the dilaton around the quantum Nariai solution using a cos x perturbation.

Nester two-form surface integrals are related to volume integrals by the divergence theorem. Replacing the gravitational spinor derivative by its supercovariant counterpart brings gauge-charge terms into the mass bound; vanishing fermion variations supplies first-order Killing-spinor equations.

For stationary configurations, reduce along the Killing time direction and apply enlarged duality-group SO(1,1) boosts to Schwarzschild or Kerr seeds. Subsequent D-dimensional dualities supply additional charge parameters while preserving the Einstein-frame metric; further transformations restore arbitrary asymptotic scalars.

Scalar-dependent gauge couplings and central charges are organized using coset representatives and symplectic embeddings. For N=2 theories, the symplectic-section formulation of special geometry works without assuming a prepotential exists in every frame; its local construction requires an invertible special-coordinate Jacobian.

Promote symmetry-breaking couplings, auxiliary heavy masses, or the supersymmetric dynamical scale to charged spurions restoring a continuous U(1). Apply continuous matching, freeze the spurions, and classify shifts from massive Dirac and Majorana fermions.

Cancel flavor anomalies with gauge-singlet spectators, weakly gauge the continuous flavor group, and compare discrete transformations of instanton-induced fermion correlators. Gravitational instantons supply a separate linear-charge constraint.

Compute the Coulomb metric from deformation kinetic energy, with g_eff^−2=2Σ_i m_i δ_i² in the stated normalization. D3-branes spanning finite faces give monopole strings whose tensions equal face areas in the chosen units.

Construct a convex integer-lattice graph dual to the web: a (p,q) edge crosses a grid line with vector ±(−q,p). Charge conservation ensures polygon closure; connected, resolved trivalent graphs permit Euler counting of finite faces.

Analyze BPS particles through string/strip webs and, after compactification, minimal-area membranes. Closed-form integrals become boundary periods; membrane boundaries must be nontrivial in H₁(S) but trivial in H₁(R²×T²). The period primitive depends on the configuration.

Retain the usual intersecting metric and field-strength form while allowing each constituent function additional dependence on its own transverse coordinates. Substitute into supergravity equations to obtain coupled differential equations and restrictions on simultaneous relative-coordinate dependence.

Analyze Killing spinors after oxidation to eleven dimensions, using the spin connection, supercovariant derivative and algebraic gamma-matrix projections. The triple-M2 example has ε=(H₁H₂H₃)^−1/6 ε₀ with constant ε₀.

Fourier-expand along compact circles and solve radial equations. Single-brane modes use modified Bessel functions; the black-hole/string example uses Kummer confluent hypergeometric functions; the NS string/NS5 example again uses modified Bessel functions.

Describe f!E using the pullback of E to a tubular normal neighborhood and a K-theoretic Thom class δ(N). The latter is represented by even/odd exterior powers with sphere-bundle isomorphism σ(s)=s∧−ι(s), extended as a relative K-class.

Define the cohomological Gysin map using Poincaré duality, apply its projection formula, then invoke an Atiyah–Hirzebruch version of differentiable Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch to express the charge through the K-theoretic pushforward f!.

Use anomaly descent and inflow at a chiral brane intersection, together with exact tangent/normal bundle sequences and multiplicativity of Â, to infer the modified worldvolume coupling. The original normal-fermion explanation is explicitly corrected in version 3.

Replace a constant symmetry parameter by compact-coordinate dependence and then apply the ordinary coordinate-independent Kaluza–Klein ansatz. For a shift-symmetric axion this is Φ̂(x,z)=Φ(x)+mz; cancellation of z dependence is checked at the level of higher-dimensional equations.

Describe twists through local bundle sections related by G-valued transition functions; use globally defined connection forms and coordinate periods to constrain compactifications. The SL(2,R) example uses (∂zλ)λ⁻¹=C, while the eleven-dimensional scaling reduction uses a Weyl rescaling to obtain curvature terms.

Encode collapsing cycles by integral normals to polytope faces. Lattice points encode monomial sections; a vertex is smooth when its vanishing cycles generate the full torus-cycle lattice. Blowups replace suitable vertices by finite faces.

Construct dual polytope or ray data, associate a Laurent monomial to each integral point, and relate face equations to monomial equations using yi=exp(xi). Local mirror geometry is expressed through a sum of these monomials with complex coefficients.

Count divisor deformations through Riemann–Roch and vanishing of higher cohomology for very ample P; obtain tensor zero modes through Chern classes, Euler characteristic and signature. Apply the large-momentum CFT entropy formula and derive membrane charges from world-volume flux couplings.

Use the N=2 attractor equations and cubic prepotential for the macroscopic area law. Evaluate the special curvature-squared term descending from eleven-dimensional R⁴ on a Euclidean black-hole geometry of Euler characteristic two to extract an entropy correction.

Supercovariantize first-order equations and fermion transformations, then impose supersymmetry-algebra closure. Closure on fermions determines their equations of motion and additional cubic terms; symplectic-Majorana and Fierz identities organize the spinor algebra.

Use a Lagrangian prescription for bosonic equations, imposing tensor (anti)self-duality only after variation. In the 1.5-order formalism the spin connection satisfies its equation and is held fixed during variations.

Determine the supersymmetry anomaly from the consistent gauge anomaly and the coupled gauge/supersymmetry Wess-Zumino conditions. Track the freedom to add supersymmetry variations of local quartic-gaugino functionals.

Construct symmetry-compatible polynomial scalar potentials and inspect their vacuum structure. A variational wall-energy argument compares a direct fundamental-wall profile with a path through an intermediate vacuum representing two D-walls.

Classify defects using the vacuum manifold M=G/H and the criterion π_(d−p−1)(M) nontrivial for a p-dimensional defect in d spatial dimensions. The examples use disconnected vacua, circle factors and a two-torus.

Use scalar phase winding, symmetry restoration in string cores and asymptotic vanishing of covariant derivatives to describe string junctions and magnetic-flux routing. These are model and topology arguments, not explicit junction-profile solutions.

Formulate rigid conformal transformations using Lorentz representations, Weyl weights, conformal Killing vectors and possible additional special-conformal terms. For actions with at most first derivatives, test special-conformal invariance separately; Poincaré and scale invariance alone do not establish it.

Present the orthosymplectic algebra using SO(6,2) triality and graded commutators, then decompose it into six-dimensional generators. Embed AdS7 as a hypersurface in eight dimensions to relate linear ambient SO(6,2) transformations to world-volume conformal transformations.

Use PST tensor gauge symmetries, the κ projector Γ²=1 and compensating transformations to derive the gauge-fixed action and supersymmetries. Obtain an explicit Wess-Zumino potential modulo total derivatives, with normalization fixed by gauge symmetry III.

Derive on-shell Ward identities from classical gauge invariance, retaining boundary terms explicitly. Use them to cancel gauge variations between gauge-field and ghost determinants, with the local measure included.

Expand the Faddeev–Popov integral about a classical extremal in relativistic gauge. Reduce gauge and ghost functional determinants to endpoint matrices using homogeneous basis solutions, Green functions, Wronskian identities and integrated variational equations.

Use the semiclassical ansatz K=P exp(iS/ℏ). Hamilton–Jacobi equations determine the leading action; quasi-continuity equations determine the one-loop prefactor for the previously proposed operator realization. Gauge fixing replaces the degenerate mixed Hessian of S by an invertible matrix.

Apply the same decoupling limit to the brane theory and its supergravity solution. Dropping the constant term in the harmonic function exposes an AdS throat; flux quantization relates its radius to brane number. Redshift shows that fixed gauge-theory energies retain finite proper wavelengths in string units.

Study a Higgsed D3 probe through its Born–Infeld action. For the scalar-only subsector, broken conformal invariance fixes a square-root functional form; no force, the protected quadratic term and the imported one-loop quartic term fix its constants. Fixing the complete action with all supersymmetries is proposed rather than demonstrated.

Use near-extremal solutions at fixed field-theory energy density. Their finite Hawking temperature and radiation into the surviving AdS region, together with field-theory unitarity, motivate inclusion of propagating supergravity states in the field-theory Hilbert space.

Analyze anomaly matching by embedding the discrete symmetry in an internally anomaly-free continuous U(1), spontaneously breaking it with auxiliary matter, and retaining the resulting massless axion contribution to the current and anomaly amplitudes.

Integrate out heavy fields in the leading adiabatic approximation, selecting the lowest-energy branch. Compare the resulting cusp potential with full-theory wall profiles; in the supersymmetric example, freeze the light field at the cusp and calculate the rapidly changing heavy-field contribution with BPS equations.
Use the centrally extended supersymmetry algebra to relate the BPS bound to endpoint gluino condensates, then examine how large-N effective-action counting can fail away from vacuum minima.

Kaluza–Klein reduction along finite D6 segments reads off gauge couplings: g_i^−2 = (x6_{i+1}−x6_i)/(g_s l_s^3) = φ6_{i+1}−φ6_i. Relative NS positions in 789 give FI triplets; relative tenth-coordinate positions give theta fields. Tensor–gauge couplings and dynamical FI/theta fields implement Green–Schwarz cancellation.

Charge bookkeeping at each NS-brane determines allowed ranks and matter. Supersymmetric brane motions, D6 reconnection, and D8–NS crossings describe Higgs transitions and brane creation; T-duality and strong-coupling M-theory lifts supply instanton interpretations.

The principal derivation integrates quantum constraints for momenta conjugate to Dirac-brane coordinates. A simultaneous double-pass is contractible in configuration space and must produce phase 2πn; orientations of the two swept surfaces supply the parity-dependent relative sign.

A Hamiltonian Legendre transformation followed by solving Gauss’s law introduces a second potential. Adding a variationally trivial term symmetrizes the electric and magnetic descriptions; the associated locally defined functional can be multivalued on configuration space.

Appendices give alternative arguments using quantized field angular momentum and compatibility of regular gauge patches. The patch connection includes contributions from the attached Dirac brane, beyond the explicit source interaction.

The paper reviews Brown–Henneaux boundary conditions, takes the quotient of allowed diffeomorphisms by those vanishing sufficiently rapidly at infinity, and imports the resulting pair of Virasoro algebras and central charge. BTZ parameters are then translated into left- and right-moving conformal levels.
Cardy’s asymptotic state-counting formula S=2π√(c nR/6)+2π√(c nL/6) is evaluated using c=3ℓ/(2G), nR+nL=ℓM, and nR−nL=J, and compared with the BTZ area entropy.

Construct holomorphic integrable systems through the period map: after choosing a local trivialization, the criterion is dp∈Sym³V*. A local prepotential has period matrix as its second derivatives; for Calabi–Yau threefolds the relevant cubic is the Yukawa cubic. Extending to Deligne cohomology uses isotropy of Abel–Jacobi images.

Use a stable degeneration of elliptic K3 into two rational elliptic surfaces meeting along an elliptic fiber. The Weierstrass middle coefficients specify the elliptic curve in the geometric recipe, while the two halves encode the E8 bundle data; selecting those halves requires two marked base points.

Describe bundle restriction data by cameral covers, spectral covers, or del Pezzo fibrations. Cameral covers are locally constrained Weyl-group Galois covers with W-equivariant evaluation maps v_λ into Z; spectral covers arise as quotients by appropriate Weyl subgroups.

Extract operator dimensions from leading nonanalytic momentum dependence, discarding analytic powers for this purpose. Extend the scalar analysis to S5 partial waves and to massive spacetime scalars, where the Bessel index is ν=√(4+m²R²).
Analyze asymptotic metric-preserving diffeomorphisms. Requiring δG_μν=O(1), δG_zμ=O(z), and δG_zz=O(1) reduces the permitted boundary vector fields to solutions of the conformal Killing equation.

Solve the linearized bulk scalar Dirichlet problem using modified Bessel K functions, normalized to unity at z=R and regular down the throat. Integrating the quadratic action by parts leaves a radial boundary flux; differentiating twice with respect to boundary sources gives two-point functions.

Regulate gravitational actions near conformal infinity and subtract local boundary counterterms; logarithmic divergences are associated with a local Weyl anomaly for even d. A separate bulk Chern–Simons variation is used to reproduce the boundary chiral current anomaly.

Construct bulk-to-boundary Green functions using upper-half-space coordinates and inversion, solve prescribed asymptotic data, and reduce quadratic on-shell actions to boundary integrals. The examples recover scalar and conserved-current two-point structures, with overall constants sometimes unspecified.

Compute higher correlators through bulk Feynman diagrams with boundary-source propagators and ordinary interior propagators. The discussion interprets collapsing bulk vertices as an OPE mechanism but does not demonstrate the general OPE assertions.

Identify induced AdS representations carried by local products. Examine Feynman diagrams and an operator-product expansion of external singleton fields to diagnose restrictions on internal-line kernels needed for physical-state coupling.
Use the dipole system (□+u)φ=b, (□+u)b=0 with a Nakanishi–Lautrup field, then construct local bilinear vector currents and stress-tensor analogues.

Test supersymmetric vacua by eliminating terms linear in constant auxiliary fields F_n and D_A. Gauge invariance extends a stationary superpotential configuration along a complexified gauge orbit; a stationary effective Kähler potential on that orbit also satisfies the D-term condition.

Generalize Seiberg's spurion method: promote τ and coefficients f_r of F to external chiral superfields, and coefficients of G to external real superfields. For a real spurion with positive scalar component, write P=Z*Z exp(V_P); a perturbative phase symmetry excludes Z from the chiral integrand.

Combine holomorphy, spurionic R-charges and real translations of τ with ordinary component-Feynman-graph counting. The counting restricts allowed chiral corrections to the original tree interactions and one-loop gauge-kinetic terms; the proof does not use supergraphs.

Start with the near-horizon M2-brane AdS4×S7 metric and quotient the transverse complex coordinates by an ADE action. For the explicit cyclic case, project S7⊂C4 onto the acted-on C² plane to describe the internal quotient through S3 fibers over a four-disk.
Obtain ADE gauge bosons from M2-branes wrapped on collapsed cycles of the ADE singularity, then reduce the resulting gauge fields on the central S3. The constant mode is retained using dim H⁰(S3)=1.

Estimate finite-UV and finite-volume corrections, then minimize their combined size subject to the proposed cutoff constraint. For coupling evolution, match S-matrices of theories with different allowed cutoff pairs in their common domain of validity.

Compare extensive field-theory entropy and thermal energy with black-hole entropy and Schwarzschild-radius estimates. Thermal scaling M ∼ L³T⁴ and S ∼ L³T³ shows why saturating the area entropy bound includes states larger than the box in Schwarzschild radius.

For D7–O7, use the Seiberg–Witten description of three mutually nonlocal seven-branes, minimize the energy of a string network, and sum its segment masses. Segment geodesics make pa+qaD linear in a real path parameter; periods and Z3 symmetry determine the proposed coefficient.

For D6–O6, lift to M-theory on the double cover of Atiyah–Hitchin space. Expand the three-form as C=ω0∧A+…, using a harmonic two-form normalized on the bolt cycle. A membrane wrapped on this minimal two-cycle supplies the charged particle, whose leading mass is membrane tension times bolt area.

Extract one-loop Klein-bottle, Möbius and cylinder tadpoles through t→0 limits, modular transformations and Poisson resummation. Collect contributions by internal-volume dependence and seek factorization into separately vanishing squares.

Embed space-group translations as Wilson-line matrices. Tadpole constraints apply to each fixed-point monodromy, not merely the global twist matrix; 95 projections use the monodromy at the brane location. Commuting Wilson lines are quantized, while noncommuting ones may vary continuously.

Use Cartan–Weyl shifts γ1,9=exp(−2πiV·H) to convert Chan–Paton projections into root conditions: gauge roots satisfy ρ·V=0 mod Z; matter from plane i satisfies ρ·V=vi mod Z. Related weight projections handle 55 and 95 sectors.
Obtain Lorentzian evolution by ψ→π/2−iψ̂. In the inflationary model, the additional continuation σ→iσ̂ and ψ→−iψ̂ supplies the open chart inside the future light cone of the symmetry center.
Solve the symmetry-reduced Euclidean Einstein equations using X=R² and r proportional to dR/dτ, then perform Kaluza–Klein reduction to a four-dimensional metric and scalar field.

Estimate tunneling through the Euclidean action difference B=SE−SEflat. For the vacuum instanton, evaluate the boundary contribution at infinity and subtract the flat-space boundary term to remove the divergence.

Approximate preminimum racetrack evolution by its dominant condensate, setting Re S=1 outside the exponential. For corrected-K potentials, also linear-fit the exponent. Derive a small correction to the noncanonical dilaton's approximate scaling trajectory.

Rewrite scalar-fluid evolution as a phase-space system using N=ln(a). Solve a potential-negligible initial stage and a subsequent scaling stage analytically, then compare approximate trajectories with numerical evolution of the condensate models.

Construct closed-string boundary states from untwisted and twisted NSNS/RR coherent states. Enforce GSO and orbifold projections, then impose open-closed consistency by rewriting closed-string exchange amplitudes as projected open-string partition functions.

Use modular transformations to identify open-string sectors, and Poisson resummation to translate winding sums into Wilson-line-shifted momenta. The surviving lowest NS modes determine the compact pair's tachyon thresholds.

Reduce spherical gravity to two-dimensional dilaton gravity. Include the scale-dependent one-loop effective action for dilaton-coupled scalars, neglect its stated (∇φ)² term, and introduce an auxiliary scalar Z to localize the anomaly action.

Expand the inverse squared two-sphere radius in Fourier modes to first order in a small perturbation. Trace apparent horizons using (∇φ)² = 0; growth of the horizon perturbation δ increases the inverse squared black-hole radius and therefore signals shrinkage.

Use the Euclidean S2 × S2 instanton and impose regularity, including vanishing perturbations at its south pole. This selects a one-dimensional solution subspace; continue along u = π/2 + iv, choosing the phase for late-time Lorentzian reality.

Take a critical continuum limit using additive coupling renormalizations and multiplicative amplitude renormalization. The continuum recursion becomes a first-order PDE solved by characteristics; inverse Laplace transformation gives a Bessel-function loop propagator. Marking identities and scaling consistency constrain the branching extension.

Count triangulations with a transfer matrix, introduce generating functions in bulk and boundary weights, and solve the resulting fractional-linear iteration exactly. Contour composition and discrete inverse Laplace transforms recover loop-length amplitudes.

Compare regulated bulk geodesic propagators with boundary short-distance operator products. A second illustration identifies the near-boundary energy divergence of a stretched string with the ultraviolet self-energy of its boundary point charge.

Count cutoff cells and U(N) field components, then use the radius–flux relation and dimensional gravitational constant. A separate thermal argument combines the imported Yang–Mills equation of state with black-hole entropy and area relations.

Introduce flux, pass to the double T-dual description with R̃i = 1/Ri and g̃ = g/(R1 R2), find the classical gauge-theory minimum, and translate its BPS mass back into original variables before taking the large-area limit.

Use the transition-function consistency condition and simple connectedness of SU(2) to construct an interpolating gauge transformation that makes both torus transition functions trivial. The transformed connection can then minimize its positive field-strength energy at zero field strength.

Use a background-field path integral Φ = Φcl + δΦ: fixed source data determine a classical background, while fluctuations are integrated over. Hamiltonian mode selection uses the Klein–Gordon inner product, conserved boundary flux and vanishing energy exchange.

In global coordinates use spherical harmonics and hypergeometric solutions adapted to the origin or boundary. Requiring the origin contribution to the on-shell action to vanish selects the regular solution; boundary conditions quantize fluctuating modes, which can be written using Jacobi polynomials.

Separate the Poincaré scalar equation into Bessel equations. For q² = k² − ω² > 0, retain interior-regular Kν and exclude exponentially growing Iν; for q² < 0, use Jν and J(−ν), replacing the second by Yν at integral ν.

Self-duality eliminates H_6mn in favor of the ten independent spatial components H_lmn. The resulting Hamiltonian and momenta give a five-dimensional covariant trace. Gauge fixing B_6n=0 and imposing the remaining constraints leave three physical polarizations, whose oscillator contributions are multiplied.

Evaluate the oscillator trace using Fock-space products. Regularize its divergent vacuum energy by a five-dimensional Fourier transform and lattice Poisson identity, removing the zero term on the original lattice. This prescription preserves SL(5,Z) and supplies the vacuum contribution needed for modular cancellation.

Factorize Z into zero-mode and oscillator contributions. Apply generalized Poisson summation to the six H_1jk zero modes while retaining a sum over four H_ijk fluxes. The zero-mode sum can also be expressed as a genus-ten Riemann theta function with zero characteristic.

For a spherical region Γ with boundary B, construct the inward-directed past null surface L. Distinguish cones ending after the initial singularity, cones reaching it, and truncated cones for regions larger than the particle horizon. Bound the entropy crossing L by the area of B.

Reduce the homogeneous bound to a particle-horizon entropy/area inequality, then use power-law scaling and standard Einstein-equation solutions. Evaluate analogous ratios for directional Kasner horizons and for spherical spatial sections using the conformal horizon coordinate χ_H.

Use Fefferman–Graham coordinates and solve Einstein's equations near the conformal boundary as an expansion in ρ. For even d, the expansion requires a ρ^(d/2) logρ term. Lower coefficients and the trace of g_(d) are covariant boundary expressions, although the full g_(d) is not.

Compute the relevant coefficients by expanding sqrt(det g) and using the radial Einstein constraint to eliminate higher trace coefficients. Organize the answer into an Euler-density contribution, conformal invariants, and a removable divergence, following the imported anomaly classification.

Cut off the bulk at ρ=ε and evaluate boundary terms there. Subtract divergent local covariant counterterms. For even d, isolate the coefficient a_(d) of −logε; its transformation under a simultaneous boundary Weyl rescaling and cutoff rescaling determines the anomaly.

Modify the orbifold action by a fermionic sign T, for example R→RT for an order-two generator. T acts trivially on spacetime bosons and by −1 on spacetime fermions. For the Z4 example, g and g³ acquire T while g² remains torsion-free.

Use factorization of Klein-bottle, annulus and Möbius-strip amplitudes to impose B_a+Σ_μ C_a^μ Tr(γ_a^μ)=0, solve for Chan–Paton matrices, and obtain open-string spectra and one-loop gauge β coefficients. The parent-theory argument uses worldsheet topology and large-N suppression of crosscaps and handles.

Relate the boundary chiral algebra to Hamiltonian reduction of the AdS Chern–Simons current algebra with boundary conditions specified by an sl2 embedding. In the stated normalization this yields c=6k, with k=Q1Q5 for the D1–D5 system.

Count boundary chiral primaries through symmetric-product cohomology, spectral flow and second-quantized generating functions. Use the elliptic genus for deformation-invariant signed counting beyond states chiral on both sides, and tensor products of single-particle representations to organize multiparticle states.

Determine S³ harmonics using S³=SO(4)/SO(3): branch six-dimensional little-group representations to SO(3), then retain sphere-isometry SO(4) representations containing those SO(3) components. Match their multiplicities to AdS-supergroup multiplets, using an oscillator construction of short SU(1,1|2) representations.

Compare timelike reductions of Type II supergravity actions and scalar cosets, tracking sign changes of form kinetic terms. Construct the starred real forms through continuation of RR potentials, C_n→−iC_n, and extend the construction formally to strings using the operation denoted i^{F_L}.

Timelike T-dualize D-brane boundary conditions and metrics, then allow the transverse harmonic function to depend on time and obey a wave equation. Analyze E4 near-light-cone geometries, global extensions and zero-slope limits; use analytic continuation and symmetry matching to motivate the proposed duality.

The reported strategy constructs a bulk action containing A(3) and A(6), couples it to the five-brane while preserving auxiliary-field symmetries, and eliminates A(6) using an algebraic part of the duality relation.

Dirac's magnetic-source construction is generalized to a Dirac six-brane with seven-dimensional worldvolume M7 and boundary M6. Its distributional form satisfies d*G(7)=*J(6). The extended strengths are Fhat(4)=dA(3)−*G(7) and Fhat(7)=dA(6)−A(3)∧dA(3)−H(3)∧*G(7).

Identify axionic dilaton vectors with positive roots in Borel gauge; compare the two reduction pictures' simple-root Dynkin diagrams to show that their coordinate-transformation subalgebras collectively generate the CJ algebra.
Reduce an enlarged ten-dimensional Lagrangian with unconstrained H(5), then impose the dimensionally reduced H(5)=*H(5) conditions and eliminate redundant fields where appropriate.

Construct explicit axion correspondences using internal linear transformations, IIA/IIB T-duality and reduced self-duality constraints. For axions obtained by dualisation, work with field strengths because dualisation is nonlocal on potentials.
Dehn twists and Sp(2h,Z) modular transformations reduce supersymmetry-breaking fermionic twist assignments to a canonical representative, while allowing induced shifts on worldsheet bosons.

Boundary analysis uses absence of physical tachyons for collapsing handles, supersymmetric one-loop tadpoles or massive intermediate states for separating degenerations, and exponential suppression by winding action at additional boundaries of the fixed-twist domain.

RNS path integrals, theta-function spin-structure sums, Riemann identities, and picture-changing correlators are used. In the chosen collision limit, the authors track zeros from spin sums and the supermoduli determinant against poles from prime forms.

Discrete Fourier transformation relates ranks to Chan–Paton traces: tr γ(n,n′)=Σ(r,s) N(r,s) exp[2πi(nr/k+n′s/k′)]. Transforming anomaly constraints diagonalizes the nondegenerate problem; transforming N(r,s)A(r,s) handles empty boxes.

The authors compute theta-function cylinder amplitudes and factorize in the closed-string channel. Separate RR tadpoles must vanish despite supersymmetric cancellation of the total amplitude. Additional twist insertions isolate bilinear amplitudes corresponding to Fourier modes of the weighted gauge anomalies.

Gauge-coupling running is extracted through Wess–Zumino couplings and, more explicitly, by turning on F23=BQ with Q in the Cartan subalgebra and expanding the cylinder amplitude to quadratic order in the background field.

Wormhole combinatorics are encoded by local terms CI∫OI and hypothetical bilocal terms CIJ∫OI(x)OJ(y). A Gaussian integral over coherent-state parameters αI rewrites the bilocal possibility as fluctuating local couplings CI+αI, with K the inverse of C.

The main consistency test equates bulk generating functionals with boundary instanton correlators. Deterministic correlators in a fixed boundary theory are argued to be incompatible with an additional average over bulk α-parameters.

The paper reviews the half-BPS axion–dilaton relation: its contribution to the Einstein-frame stress tensor vanishes, leaving AdS5×S5 unchanged. The remaining configuration is specified by a harmonic function, taken homogeneous on S5, and examined after transformation to string frame.

A proposed order-1/N repair uses a retarded Green function in a Yang–Feldman equation plus a homogeneous correction φ1. A cancellation condition would remove the pre-existing connected CFT three-point contribution and leave the local supergravity result.

An LSZ-like spatial boundary limit multiplies each external bulk leg by r raised to its asymptotic conformal power before taking r→∞. The paper uses this to relate reconstructed-field correlators to GKP/W boundary correlators, subject to unresolved limit and integration subtleties.

Large-N factorization and conformal representation theory identify single-trace frequency modes with creation and annihilation operators. A harmonic expansion using normalizable bulk wavefunctions constructs φ(x)=∫G(x,b)O(b), with G solving the homogeneous Klein–Gordon equation.

Compute cylinder, Möbius-strip, and Klein-bottle contributions; factor their sum into twisted tadpole conditions. Expand trigonometric factors in exponentials to express these conditions as Fourier transforms of the one-loop beta-function coefficients.

Construct orientifold groups and Chan–Paton representations, impose the group algebra, and extract the projected D3-brane spectra. Relate the opposite-charge extension to a half-shift on the T-dual Taub–NUT circle.

Check twisted ground-state level matching and, for even-order elements, the additional mod-two condition. Choose shifts outside the dual invariant lattice I* to avoid unwanted massless twisted states; where shifts vanish, count twisted states explicitly.

At special Narain points choose a simply laced rank-d algebra G and Γd,d(G)={(pL,pR):pL,pR∈ΛW(G), pL−pR∈ΛR(G)}. Classify Weyl-group twists with appropriate Spin(d) action, then choose shifts compatible with modular invariance.

Use flux conservation and Schwarz inequalities to bound integrated matter energy by charge-dependent terms. Independently apply the second variation of minimal-surface area, Gauss–Codazzi, and Gauss–Bonnet to derive topology and area constraints.

Evolve level surfaces with normal speed vn=1/p, giving dA/ds=A. Use f=∫S(4KG−p²−4Λ/3)dA and the local inequality d(f√A)/ds≥√A∫S16πT00. The stated equality conditions are constant p on each leaf and vanishing trace-free second fundamental form.

Evaluate a BPS particle’s Schwinger one-loop determinant in a constant self-dual graviphoton background; sum KK charges using a Fourier delta-comb identity and use product/logarithm identities to reorganize the result.

Expand the exact SU(N) Chern–Simons partition function on S³ at large N, using the sine product and zeta sums; identify open-string coefficients and analytically extrapolate the number of boundaries toward zero.

Construct flux bundles with clock-and-shift matrices and explicit translation operators. Identify the algebras of adjoint modes on dual tori to derive Morita transformations, trace rescaling and electric-flux quantization from global gauge transformations.

Legendre-transform the abelian Born–Infeld action, package electric, magnetic and momentum densities into three-vectors, and obtain BPS masses as an energy lower bound using the enhanced three-dimensional metric.

Riemann identities evaluate spin-structure sums. Local prime-form expansions, determinant zeros, Taylor expansions and operator-exchange parity then distinguish vanishing contributions, finite collision terms and surviving poles.

Delta-function gravitino support converts supermoduli integration into picture-changing-operator correlators with ghost and determinant factors. The specialized gauge imposes z1+z2=2Δγ, chooses γ and κ odd, and then takes z1,z2→Δγ.

Use separated-brane position-space propagators and dimensional analysis to estimate finite bulk-loop soft masses. Heavy bulk exchange is exponentially suppressed by propagation across the compact dimension.

Isolate the supergravity scalar auxiliary background, rescale visible chiral fields, and track super-Weyl and Konishi anomalies through cutoff-dependent couplings. Expand wavefunction renormalization in the background superfield; Appendix B illustrates the mechanism with regulated SQED.

Use Iwasawa decomposition and the full relevant solvable Lie algebra to parameterize scalar cosets. Match its generator commutators to dimensional-reduction field strengths; mere embedding into a larger algebra does not establish an effective action of that larger group.

Construct constrained matrix representatives M=VᵀV with VᵀΩV=Ω, and compare the scalar trace Lagrangian with vector kinetic couplings. Dualize antisymmetric tensor potentials using Lagrange multipliers and Bianchi identities.

Approximate K3 by resolving T⁴/Z₂ with sixteen Eguchi–Hanson spaces. Use harmonic two-forms and Lichnerowicz metric zero modes for reduction, then wrapped-brane flux integrals and Dirac quantization for charge matching.
Thom/Bott constructions use normal spinor bundles and Clifford multiplication T=Γ·x. Spin^c bundles replace spin bundles when the normal bundle has an integral lift of w2.
Stable equivalence of bundle pairs implements addition or removal of identical brane–antibrane bundles. Tubular-neighborhood gluing and stabilization extend localized tachyon data to spacetime.

Dirac indices and fermion-zero-mode quantization diagnose Type I defects. Worldsheet constructions add a boundary fermion η for the zerobrane and use GSO and orientation projections to analyze tachyons.

For S2×S2, linearizes the eleven-dimensional Einstein equations in de Donder gauge and expands in product harmonics. Separates traceless deformations of each sphere from opposite-volume breathing fluctuations, while accounting for fixed flux.

Uses radial equations and infrared asymptotics for the deformed metric. Nambu–Goto and D1 minimal-area calculations give electric and magnetic loop diagnostics; the reported large-separation electric force scales as L^−2.

Parametrizes the E6(6)/Sp(4) scalar coset, expands the gauged potential to quadratic order with canonical kinetic terms, removes Higgs-eaten scalars, and compares resulting masses with the AdS stability bound.

Double-line counting organizes gauge diagrams by genus and number of holes. The authors resum the hole expansion of the exact Chern–Simons free energy and compare it with constant-map and multiple-cover contributions to closed A-model amplitudes.

Gravitational Chern–Simons counterterms are compared with boundary-dependent regularizations of closed-string characteristic-class integrals. HOMFLY skein relations test the genus and instanton structure expected for Wilson loops.

Higgs/Coulomb branch analysis of the linear sigma model motivates integrating out Coulomb patches as holes with Dirichlet boundaries. A vortex-sector argument is offered for their weights, explicitly as speculation.

Apply harmonic-function superposition, S-duality and Buscher-type T-duality rules to obtain a heuristic metric map. Analyze the strong-coupling lift using holomorphic M5 curves, degeneration of meromorphic coefficients and genus/moduli counting.

Use holomorphic KK-monopole separation and T-duality along x6 to construct the NS5/D4 system; read gauge factors and bifundamental matter from D4 segments and strings crossing NS5-branes. Integrate out rotation-induced massive adjoints to obtain a quartic superpotential.

Project onto gauge singlets by integrating 1/det(1−zR(g)) over the group. The Weyl form reduces this to rank-many contour integrals, with a root product in the numerator, a representation-weight product in the denominator and a factor 1/|W|.

For low-order coefficients, differentiate in z and set z=0 before taking contour residues, reducing poles to the origin. An extended-weight index formula is also quoted; Schur functions and the MacMahon algorithm are suggested as possible computational alternatives.

Restrict the invariant potential to group singlets. The authors invoke Schur's lemma: variations in nonsinglet directions have no linear term, so a critical point within the singlet manifold is also critical in the full scalar space.

Construct the 27×27 E6(6) scalar matrix using vector and spinor representations, rotate into the SL(6,R)×SL(2,R) basis, and assemble the potential with Mathematica. Critical-point supersymmetry is determined by comparing Wab eigenvalues with the cosmological-constant criterion.

Spherically symmetric Euclidean probe-brane trajectories follow from conserved Euclidean energy and are continued to Lorentzian evolution. The Brill analysis uses harmonic Einstein–Maxwell solutions and a vacuum-subtracted boundary action.

The paper takes near-horizon scaling limits, integrates the two-dimensional gravity–dilaton null constraint across AdS2, and scales known slow-motion multicentre actions to obtain throat moduli-space dynamics.

Generalize the Schwinger proper-time one-loop determinant to BPS particles in a constant self-dual graviphoton background. Supersymmetry and an imported heterotic one-loop expression determine spin-dependent contributions to the R+² couplings.

Quantize twisted wrapped-brane zero modes. In the D2 description, study cohomology of the curve-deformation space enlarged by flat connections, using Lefschetz actions to infer spin; multiwrapping introduces moduli of nonabelian flat connections.
Express left-spin content in the basis Ir=([1/2]+2[0])^r, sum circle momenta, and use a delta-function rewriting of that sum to obtain the winding/multicover expansion of the topological amplitude.

Classify proton-decay operators through representatives QQQL^(k+1)H+^k N^m and QQQL^(k+1)H+^k(N*)^m. Charge-preserving substitutions relate other channels to these representatives; their two discrete charges differ by one and cannot both vanish modulo 3. Higgs insertions are retained; F± are excluded as too heavy.

Construct anomaly-free parent U(1) symmetries before taking discrete remnants: add oppositely charged Standard-Model singlets of charges ±N and assume a flat direction with nonzero VEVs. This addresses mixed Abelian anomalies that require information about the massive spectrum.

Affine ADE quivers motivate constituent instanton charges. Holomorphy and the unit-instanton factor exp(2πiτ) then constrain fractional-instanton actions and the proposed superpotential. These are author arguments rather than a direct membrane path-integral calculation.

The spectrum calculation uses seven-dimensional ADE super Yang–Mills on M×R4, identifying its Spin(3) R-symmetry with the spin cover of M's structure group. Twisted fields become differential forms, and their four-dimensional massless modes are counted through Laplacian zero modes.

The argument decomposes open-string excitations into NN, DD and DN boundary-condition sectors, then uses a zero-slope limit and supersymmetry protection of massless short multiplets to transfer the relevant spectrum between dual descriptions.
Field parities and invariance of brane Wess-Zumino couplings determine the extension of world-sheet parity Ω to BPS branes. Conjugation by IIB S-duality then defines Ω̃ = SΩS⁻¹.

Construct the even space from Killing vectors and the odd space from Killing spinors. The even action uses the Kosmann derivative L_VΨ=∇_VΨ−(1/4)(∇_iV_j)γ^{ij}Ψ, which preserves Killing spinors with the same λ.

For spinors with the same λ, the bilinear V^i=〈Ψ,γ^iΞ〉 supplies a Killing vector. The paper uses Grassmann-odd field-theory spinors to explain symmetry of the odd bracket. The remaining three-odd Jacobi identity is a separate condition, expressible through Fierz rearrangements; it is not established universally by this construction.

Establish discrete anomaly freedom by embedding the discrete group in an explicitly anomaly-free continuous parent. This avoids relying solely on light-spectrum discrete anomaly tests, since mixed Abelian anomalies can depend on massive states and parent-symmetry breaking.

Constrain dimension-six four-fermion invariants, rotate from flavor to mass bases, and estimate additional operators using flavon VEV insertions. Approximate unitarity of first-two-generation rotation blocks controls residual flavor violation.

The two-point transition kernel is represented schematically by a sum over curves with branches and a path integral weighted by exp(iS). In the stated Born approximation the sum is restricted to smooth curves; a 2 → 2 process supplies the illustrative construction.

The paper recalls in/out operators, LSZ reduction of time-ordered Green functions, perturbative Feynman diagrams, and an on-shell functional integral with prescribed asymptotic field behavior. Their flat-space equivalence is imported background; the author warns that curved backgrounds can lead to different prescriptions.

An intuitive first-quantized construction replaces flat-space external plane waves by asymptotic AdS kernels and combines them with bulk transition kernels and invariant volume measures. The connected pre-S-matrix is expressed using classical wave solutions and their envelope factors.
Orbifold projection restricts parent N = 4 fields by Φα = gβα γg⁻¹Φβγg for every g in Γ. The action on the R-symmetry index is combined with a chosen representation γg acting on color indices.

The argument inserts Γ-invariance projectors into planar ’t Hooft diagrams and applies the imported planar-inheritance result. The self-dual and purely electric daughters are distinguished through their different color representations of the same central Z2.

Starting from the Brown–York variation, T^{μν} = 2(−γ)^(−1/2) δS/δγμν, the authors add intrinsic boundary counterterms. The resulting tensor is (8πG)⁻¹[Θ^{μν}−Θγ^{μν}+2(−γ)^(−1/2)δSct/δγμν]. On shell, only boundary terms enter the action variation.

Charges are computed as Qξ = ∫Σ√σ uμTμνξν for boundary Killing vectors. Anomaly calculations use radial metric expansions determined by Einstein's equations; the AdS3 transformation calculation uses diffeomorphisms preserving Brown–Henneaux asymptotics.

The stated counterterm densities are −√(−γ)/ℓ for AdS3, −2√(−γ)(1−ℓ²R/4)/ℓ for AdS4, and −3√(−γ)(1−ℓ²R/12)/ℓ for AdS5. Curvatures are intrinsic to γ; varying these terms supplies the boundary-metric and Einstein-tensor subtractions.

Integrates out angular coordinates and the magnetic Maxwell field, then includes the scale-dependent one-loop effective action of dilaton-coupled scalars. An auxiliary scalar Z gives a local anomaly-action representation; its homogeneous freedom supplies initial-data freedom needed by the constraints.

Expands the sphere-size perturbation in Fourier modes, using e^(2φ) = B[1 + 2εσn(t) cos(nx)] and a linear mode equation. Studies early-time power series, late-time asymptotics, and Euclidean-regular perturbations; regularity at the instanton's South pole requires σn(0) = 0 in Euclidean coordinate u and selects the Lorentzian phase.

Uses the smooth Euclidean S2 × S2 charged Nariai instanton. Its action −2π/B is normalized against the de Sitter action −3π/Λ. Neglecting a prefactor, the quoted nucleation suppression ranges from exp(−π/Λ) at zero charge toward exp(−2π/Λ) at the upper charge limit.

Selects nonseparable harmonic functions to represent localization. The paper cautions that additive or multiplicative separation can instead fail to match a delta-function brane source or describe objects delocalized in other directions.

Takes the near-core background H2 = Q/z^(r−2), initially assumes radial x dependence for H1, and changes variables to weighted radial differential equations with explicit nonseparable solutions. The construction is then generalized to relative-position centres xi and summed over them at common z0.

With the usual BPS harmonic-superposition metric ansatz, the equations are Δz H1 + H2 Δx H1 = 0 and Δz H2 + H1 Δy H2 = 0, accompanied by the constraint ∂x H1 ∂y H2 = 0. Choosing constituent 2 delocalized reduces its equation to Δz H2 = 0.

The mirror principle transports equivariant characteristic classes from stable-map graph spaces to a toric linear sigma model. Gluing identities define Euler data; linked Euler data are compared through hypergeometric mirror transformations without constructing a B-model mirror.

Explicit Atiyah–Bott localization represents fixed maps by decorated graphs, divides characteristic-class weights by normal Euler classes, and includes map automorphism factors. The authors report direct low-degree checks at degrees 1, 2, and 3.

Excess intersection assigns a positive-dimensional zero locus Y the contribution ∫_Y c(E)/c(N_{Y/M}), under the stated smooth-submanifold simplification. Virtual classes and deformation invariance extend the interpretation to the singular-map example.

Evaluate localized singularity mass and three-form charge couplings on the unperturbed background, neglecting backreaction. A separate asymptotically flat force argument diagnoses attraction versus repulsion; it does not directly compute the field-theory potential.

Construct an approximate background by orbifolding a harmonic-function supergravity solution for two mirror clusters, each containing N M2-branes. Promote the cluster separation to a slowly varying collective coordinate to extract its effective action.

The missing-state argument examines an ADHM U(1) quotient with Q5 charged hypermultiplets and an FI deformation. For positive FI parameter the local space is T*CP^{Q5−1}; its middle-dimensional L² harmonic form is followed toward the conical limit.

The quantitative long-string analysis uses Wakimoto free fields, lightcone-like gauge fixing, BRST cohomology, and a twisted spacetime stress tensor. A separate physical-gauge construction uses spin fields and an explicit N=4 superconformal algebra.

A large-brane probe action combines tension times area with a negative Wess–Zumino volume term. Covariant near-boundary expansions identify a conformal scalar for boundary dimension D>2 and a Liouville field for D=2.

Expand the normal-ordered improved stress tensor in a small pair-creation kernel F(k,k′), initially choosing opposite momenta. Separate terms linear and quadratic in F, then examine a bilocal two-point observable and conformally transformed waves.

Linearized transverse-traceless gravitational perturbations are reduced to a minimally coupled massless-scalar equation. Normalizable solutions behave as Φ ∼ z⁴ and are expanded in J2 Bessel modes; Bessel orthogonality expresses wave energy in boundary Fourier data.

Set fermionic supersymmetry variations to zero to obtain scalar gradient-flow and warp-factor equations. The connecting trajectory is found numerically, with analytic endpoint expansions; the authors report no analytic solution for the full trajectory.

Compute quadratic fluctuation masses, including kinetic metrics, super-Higgs gauge fixing and vector–tensor mixing, then apply AdS mass–dimension relations and organize fields into SU(2,2|1) × SU(2)I representations.
Use supersymmetric beta-function constraints and R-current anomaly matching to calculate endpoint a and c. The imported field-theory fixed-point argument uses γ1 = γ2 = −1/4 and γ3 = 1/2.

Evaluate generalized Green–Schwarz contributions by trigonometric identities and Fourier sums; use the non-Abelian anomaly equations to establish the required factorization of Abelian and mixed gravitational anomalies.

Compute spectra using Chan–Paton shifts and Cartan–Weyl roots, derive non-Abelian anomaly constraints on ranks, then use discrete Fourier transforms to express these constraints in twist-matrix traces for comparison with tadpole equations.

Use field redefinitions to normalize L = 1, construct an adiabatic solution and its first displacement δX, and solve separable p = f(ϕ)g(X) models for exact power-law backgrounds. Scalar stability is examined through the Laplacian coefficient in the perturbation equation.
Study the expanding-branch master equation ε̇ = −3√ε(ε+p) using parametric equation-of-state curves and phase-space attractors. For p(X), extrema at nonzero field velocity give p = −ε fixed points.

Add an intrinsic-curvature boundary counterterm to the bulk and extrinsic-curvature boundary actions. Its coefficients are fixed by requiring finite Schwarzschild-AdS action; the prescription is motivated by AdS/CFT boundary ultraviolet counterterms.
Obtain conserved charges from variation of the total action with respect to the boundary metric, contracted with boundary Killing fields. Evaluate entropy on each solution through S=βH∞−I_T.

Impose regularity in the angular and radial-time sections. Use V(r+)=0 to determine m, then equate the two required Euclidean-time periods, producing a quartic constraint on r+ or a cubic constraint in the flat limit.

Quantize the canonical modes using minimal-fluctuation initial conditions. Match short- and long-wavelength solutions through an approximately de Sitter Bessel equation for slow roll; solve the power-law case with Hankel functions.

Infer the quadratic perturbation action from its equations of motion, rather than explicitly performing the cumbersome constrained second-order expansion. Fix its remaining normalization by comparison with known scalar and hydrodynamical actions; introduce v=zζ.
Use longitudinal-gauge scalar perturbations and the linearized 00 and 0i Einstein constraints, then change variables from Φ and δϕ/ϕ̇ to ξ and ζ to simplify the dynamics.

Compare discriminant splitting and monodromies with possible tessellations in flat coordinates, using the special Kähler metric. A separate Berger–Simons holonomy argument supplies a sufficient geometric condition for global quotient moduli spaces.

Translate heterotic coupling corrections into type IIA world-sheet instantons and compute through mirror symmetry. Hypergeometric period systems, ratios defining flat coordinates, and the monomial-divisor mirror map relate algebraic parameters to geometric limits.

Approximate the string partition function by the exponential of the classical on-shell supergravity action. Expand in boundary sources to compute correlators using tree diagrams and bulk-to-boundary propagators; absorption calculations provide another route through two-point functions and the optical theorem.

Review the fixed-λ 't Hooft expansion using adjoint double-line diagrams and associated oriented surfaces. Vertices contribute N/λ, propagators λ/N and closed index loops N; the SU(N) propagator correction is treated as subleading.

Organize bulk states and CFT operators in conformal representations. Use radial quantization and the state–operator correspondence, and compare the discrete global-AdS spectrum with the CFT on R×S^p using H=(P₀+K₀)/2.

Extract tachyons and massless states from one-loop open-string vacuum amplitudes. Modular transformations of cylinder, Möbius-strip and Klein-bottle contributions isolate closed-channel R-R tadpole divergences.

Sum chiral-fermion anomaly polynomials using representation trace identities, remove irreducible sixth-order gauge terms, and factor the remaining twelve-form for cancellation by B-dependent Green–Schwarz counterterms.

For amplitudes with mixed brane boundaries, propose an extra minus sign for every spin-structure cut endpoint on an anti-D9 boundary. Cut-deformation arguments are used to motivate the reversed mixed-sector GSO projection and anti-D9 Ramond Ω projection.
Raychaudhuri’s equation, vanishing vorticity and null convergence give dθ/dλ≤−θ²/2. A negative θ₀ focuses within affine interval 2/|θ₀|; the author uses caustics as light-sheet endpoints.

Quantitative tests combine spherical mass and horizon relations with Bekenstein’s entropy/mass bound; the collapse test additionally uses Birkhoff’s theorem, a thin-shell approximation and radial-state box counting.

Slice spacetime into a one-parameter family of null hypersurfaces and project each slice to screens. For spherical examples, Penrose diagrams and apparent horizons determine projection directions and generate screen-hypersurfaces, whose causal character may vary.

Use causal containment and the second law to motivate spacelike projection. For evaporation, use null focusing and Raychaudhuri-based reasoning to suggest how infalling density profiles could affect horizon motion and outgoing radiation.

Invert the light-sheet construction: follow generators of a null hypersurface in a direction of nonnegative expansion, stopping before expansion becomes negative. The terminating surface is a screen; it is preferred if expansion vanishes everywhere on it.

A-model: evaluate the canonical-bundle obstruction contribution using virtual equivariant localization. Fixed loci are encoded by genus-, degree- and fixed-point-decorated graphs; divide by graph automorphisms and edge covering factors. Faber's recursive intersection algorithm uses descendant, Hodge and boundary classes.

Fix the genus-g holomorphic ambiguity by matching localization invariants in the first 2g − 1 degrees. An additional imported conifold prescription gives its leading coefficient as B_(2g)/[2g(2g − 2)] for higher genus, in a specified gauge; localization corroborates this prescription at g = 2, 3.

B-model: integrate holomorphic-anomaly recursions using Kodaira–Spencer propagators. Reconstruct periods and Yukawa couplings from Picard–Fuchs equations, use Meijer-function analytic continuation in local P², and obtain the mirror map from the logarithmic period because the analytic solution is constant.

Separate linearized tensor fluctuations into four-dimensional momentum modes and extra-dimensional profiles, then transform their equation into a one-dimensional Schrödinger-type problem with an attractive delta function and a decaying barrier.

Use Bessel-function solutions, small-mass brane boundary conditions, and large-distance plane-wave asymptotics. Finite-volume quantization supplies the continuum measure dm when the regulator is removed.

Compute static brane-source exchange using the zero mode and massive propagators; assess nonlinear limitations through the position-dependent cubic graviton interaction and the zero-mode probability at large z.
Use compactly supported cohomology, Poincaré duality, intersection lattices, and the exact sequence of (X,∂X) to distinguish allowed fluxes, domain-wall changes, and invariant boundary data.

Find wrapped BPS cycles by calibrated-volume minimization. For the A-series n-fold model, dW=P_m(z1)^((n−2)/2)dz1 maps candidate cycles to straight segments in the W-plane; compare the resulting solitons with Landau-Ginzburg models.

Apply quasihomogeneous scaling to norms of Ω and its Gauss-Manin derivatives, determining finite-distance conditions, vanishing Hodge components, and whether deformation modes have finite kinetic energy.

Analyze exponential racetrack superpotentials and conditions W = W′ = 0; use R-symmetry spurions for nonrenormalizable gauge operators to expose additional, potentially unsuppressed terms in the condensate expansion.
Estimate nonholomorphic corrections by loop counting with a species factor N² and a cutoff-dependent factor Λ²/Mp², comparing weak heterotic, strongly coupled heterotic, and Type I scale relations.

Calculate the alternative negative-energy inward-tunneling channel by reversing time and using the antiparticle contour prescription. For the conductor comparison, use image charges to include the emitted charge's back-reaction.

Evaluate Im S=Im∫p_r dr by inserting Hamilton's equation and changing the momentum integral to an energy integral with H=M−ω′. A contour prescription evaluates the horizon pole and supplies the semiclassical tunneling exponent.

Use horizon-regular radial null geodesics, replacing M by M−ω for a positive-energy self-gravitating outgoing shell at fixed total mass. This shell prescription is imported from earlier Hamiltonian-gravity work.

Compares horizon trajectories and areas in de Sitter space and closed Robertson–Walker cosmologies. The closed-universe discussion uses the horizon coordinate χ(t)=∫₀ᵗdt′/R(t′) and an equation-of-state parameter γ.
Estimates maximal entropy using a hypothetical black hole containing the horizon's energy, with Mmax(t)∼ρ(t)H⁻³∼ρ(t)Ep³, then compares its entropy with horizon area using cosmological scaling laws.

Families of Dirac operators, real KO-theory indices, boundary-symbol index comparison, and excision reduce the sign anomaly to a boundary mod-2 index. Doubling converts the boundary problem into a twisted chiral problem on closed surfaces.

Geometric index theory computes determinant/Pfaffian curvature and holonomy through exponentiated η-invariants and flat index theorems. Čech cocycles describe the global A- and B-field data and their anomaly-canceling relation.

Construct torus partition functions using SU(2) affine characters, the Feigin–Fuchs sector, and the gauge-lattice theta function. Import the ADE classification of SU(2) modular invariants to organize candidate heterotic models.

Build scalar Neveu–Schwarz vertex operators satisfying supercurrent primarity, dimensions (1,1), and locality with spacetime supercharges. Left-moving current-algebra descendants generate chiral-primary representations; orbifold sectors are constrained by level matching and mutual locality.

Construct torus, Klein-bottle, annulus, and Möbius amplitudes using SO(4) characters. Impose closed-sector modular invariance, crosscap consistency, open-spectrum positivity, and RR tadpole cancellation; use S and P transformations between channels.

Read massless representations from direct-channel amplitudes, evaluate gauge/gravitational anomaly cancellation, and factorize the remaining NS tadpoles to infer a string-frame scalar potential. Transverse-channel perfect squares organize boundary and crosscap couplings.

Analyze warped Kaluza–Klein fluctuations and lift flux through a shrinking elliptic fiber. Apply Buscher T-duality along two torus isometries, followed by type-I/heterotic S-duality, to obtain local metrics, dilatons, and torsion fields.

Use the reviewed eleven-dimensional supersymmetry equations, Hodge type, primitivity, and self-duality of G. Construct quantized fluxes using K3 intersection lattices and toroidal forms, testing orbifold periods and twisted-sector intersections separately.

Subtract charged vertex-operator weights from total conformal weights, apply the CFT entropy formula to the remaining neutral excitations, and compare its BPS specialization with the E7(7) quartic invariant.

Use the M-theory supersymmetry central-charge eigenvalue equation, Clifford-matrix projections, and expansion in the charge hierarchy for right-moving excitation energies; use global symmetries for left-moving weights.

Extremize the background mass over moduli to distinguish fixed scalars from free hypermultiplet scalars. Restricted SL(3)/SO(3) metric sectors and charge matrices make more general backgrounds explicitly tractable.
Represent background dependence through nonabelian Taylor expansions and compare linear D0-brane multipole couplings with matrix-theory expressions to select a trace prescription.

T-dualize the D9-brane Born–Infeld action along 9−p isometric directions, retaining covariant-derivative terms that become scalar commutators. Interior products generate the corresponding Chern–Simons commutator couplings.

Extremize the leading quartic-plus-cubic scalar potential using SU(2) matrix representations, then compare radius, energy, and dipole coupling with an abelian spherical D2 Born–Infeld/Chern–Simons calculation.

A nilpotent gauge charge defines graded variations. Gauge invariance is imposed inductively as d_Q T_n equal to divergences of products with one Q-vertex; local anomalies are tested for cancellation by local normalization terms.

Epstein–Glaser induction constructs time-ordered operator-valued distributions by Wick expansion and retarded/advanced splitting of causal numerical distributions. Nonnegative singular order requires subtracted dispersion integrals and permits local derivative-of-delta normalization terms.

Reduce the six-dimensional small-instanton theory on the P¹ base. The nontrivial K3 fibration twists the Dirac operator and preserves one covariantly constant spinor. Coupling and volume scaling then test simultaneous gravitational, world-sheet and gauge perturbativity.
Use heterotic/Type I duality to evaluate the small-instanton coupling: λ_I=1/λ_H and l_I²=λ_H l_H² turn g_D5²=(2π)³λ_I l_I² into g_SI²=(2π)³l_H², independent of the heterotic dilaton.

Pull back the bulk metric to the moving brane, replace bulk time with brane proper time, and read off a Friedmann-like expansion equation. Effective density and pressure are defined from this induced evolution rather than supplied as four-dimensional gravitational sources.

Solve the bosonic DBI plus Wess–Zumino dynamics in static gauge, using conserved Hamiltonian and angular momentum to obtain first integrals for radial and angular motion. The effective radial problem can be solved by quadratures.

Geometric Euler-characteristic computations, nodal stratifications and proposed reducible-curve corrections supply data to fix B-model holomorphic ambiguities; mirror symmetry and localization provide comparison calculations.

Abel–Jacobi maps and multiplication by the Jacobian theta class relate curve Hilbert schemes to spin data. Taking alternating cohomological traces gives formulas involving Euler characteristics of relative Hilbert schemes.
The imported Schwinger one-loop interpretation relates five-dimensional BPS particles to four-dimensional self-dual curvature/graviphoton couplings; circle momenta produce the multicover sum.

Quasihomogeneous scaling and the singularity ring classify deformations. An imported perturbative worldsheet construction adds a negatively charged LG field, fixes total ĉ=d, and applies a Gepner projection; constant deformation gives an SL(2)/U(1) factor.

Winding-index contradictions establish path uniqueness; minimization of ∫|√P dx| establishes connectivity by BPS segments. Local root geometry and charge-phase alignment determine decay across marginal stability.

Represent a three-sphere as an S² fibration over a root-to-root path in the x-plane. Supersymmetry requires constant phase of √P(x)dx, equivalently a straight image under its integral, or dx/dt=α/√P(x).

Use Friedmann solutions and particle-horizon estimates, including an Euler beta-function expression at maximal expansion, to compare entropy-to-boundary ratios at the turning point and near final collapse.

Model entropy as S=n_H S^H, n_H=(a|H|)^2, S^H=|H|^α. The condition dS/dt≥0 becomes 2H+(2+α)Ḣ/H≥0; Einstein equations convert this into pressure constraints, while the first law supplies a temperature expression.

Gauge-group restrictions are extracted from the cubic tensor and its symplectic tensor representation. The partial classification uses Jordan-algebra models, real Clifford-algebra descriptions of homogeneous spaces, and constructions from symmetric group d-symbols and symplectic representation matrices.
